results.question: Why might a UE need to acquire system information other than MIB and SIB1?
results.reference: To obtain other SIBs that are not scheduled in SIB1 but are required for the UE's operation, such as those containing cell access parameters or configuration for other RATs.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2, System information acquisition
results.model_answer: A UE may need SI beyond MIB and SIB1 because those messages provide only the minimum information to identify/access the cell and to discover how other SI is provided. Parameters needed for a specific operation—such as cell reselection evaluation, inter-frequency mobility, access restrictions, warning-message reception, or support of an optional feature—may reside in other SIBs. The UE therefore acquires the scheduled or on-demand SI indicated by SIB1 when that information is needed; it need not acquire every SIB unconditionally.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2 (Acquisition of system information), together with clause 5.2.1 (General): SIB1 provides scheduling/availability information for other SI, while a UE acquires the applicable SystemInformation message(s) when it needs SIBs other than MIB and SIB1.

results.question: How does a UE acquire system information that is not broadcast?
results.reference: The UE requests the specific system information from the network using an on-demand mechanism, if supported and configured by SIB1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2, System information acquisition
results.model_answer: For SI marked as notBroadcast in SIB1 scheduling information, the UE uses the on-demand SI procedure. It obtains the SI-request configuration from SIB1, initiates the configured random-access/SI-request procedure (using the configured PRACH occasion/preamble and, where applicable, an RRCSystemInfoRequest on UL-CCCH identifying the requested SIBs), and then monitors for the requested SystemInformation message. The gNB delivers the requested SI on DL-SCH, normally scheduled with SI-RNTI. A request obtains the SI message containing the requested SIB(s), not necessarily only one individual SIB.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3/5.2.2.4 (Acquisition of other SI / SI request procedure; clause numbering may vary slightly by release). Relevant ASN.1 is in TS 38.331 clause 6.3.2 (SIB1 and SI-RequestConfig) and clause 6.2.2 (RRCSystemInfoRequest). The procedure distinguishes SI with si-BroadcastStatus = broadcast from SI with si-BroadcastStatus = notBroadcast, for which the UE performs an SI request using the configuration carried by SIB1.

results.question: What specific procedure must a UE execute, and with what release cause, when it reselects to an inter-RAT cell?
results.reference: The UE must perform the actions specified for going to RRC_IDLE, using the release cause 'other'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.12, Inter RAT cell reselection
results.model_answer: Upon reselection to an inter-RAT cell, the UE shall perform the RRC connection release procedure with the release cause set to "other".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.4.3 (Actions related to RRC release): the UE behaviour for inter-RAT cell reselection specifies performing RRC connection release with release cause "other" (exact subclause numbering may vary slightly by release/version).

results.question: Upon completing inter-RAT cell reselection, which clause defines the subsequent actions the UE shall take?
results.reference: The UE shall follow the actions in clause 5.3.11 for going to RRC_IDLE, applying the release cause 'other'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.12, Inter RAT cell reselection
results.model_answer: TS 38.331 clause 5.2.4.8, "Actions upon cell reselection," defines the subsequent UE actions after completing inter-RAT cell reselection.
results.evidence: The RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE cell-selection-and-reselection procedure directs the UE to apply the actions specified in clause 5.2.4.8 after reselection; this includes the applicable RAT-dependent handling following an inter-RAT reselection.

results.question: How does the initiating UE determine whether to include ue-CapabilityInformationSidelink in the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message?
results.reference: The initiating UE decides autonomously based on its own needs, as the specification states it is up to the initiating UE to decide whether to include it.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.2.3, Actions related to transmission of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: The initiating UE includes ue-CapabilityInformationSidelink only when it has sidelink UE-capability information to provide to the responding UE as part of the capability exchange. It constructs that information from its supported sidelink capabilities (for the relevant RAT, normally NR) and includes it in the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink when the procedure requires/provides for reciprocal capability delivery. The ue-CapabilityRAT-RequestList is used to request the responding UE's capabilities; it is not, by itself, an instruction to include the initiating UE's capability information. If the initiating UE has no applicable sidelink capability information to provide, the optional ue-CapabilityInformationSidelink is omitted.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause covering the sidelink UE capability enquiry/transfer procedure (typically under clause 5.7, "Sidelink", with exact subclause numbering depending on release) and the ASN.1 definition of UECapabilityEnquirySidelink/UECapabilityEnquirySidelink-r16-IEs. The procedure specifies the initiating-UE actions for populating ue-CapabilityRAT-RequestList and conditionally including ue-CapabilityInformationSidelink; the ASN.1 marks the capability-information element as optional/conditional.

results.question: What mandatory field must always be included when the initiating UE transmits a UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message, and what is its purpose?
results.reference: The initiating UE must always include the frequencyBandListFilterSidelink field, which specifies the frequency bands for which the peer UE is requested to provide supported bands and band combinations.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.2.3, Actions related to transmission of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: The initiating UE shall include ue-CapabilityRAT-RequestList-r16 (the UE-CapabilityRAT-RequestList IE). It identifies the RAT capability/capabilities—particularly the sidelink-relevant RAT capability information—that the peer UE is requested to report in its UECapabilityInformationSidelink response.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.2 (Sidelink UE capability transfer), especially the initiation procedure, together with the ASN.1 definition of UECapabilityEnquirySidelink-r16-IEs in clause 6.3. The ue-CapabilityRAT-RequestList-r16 IE is mandatory in the message IE sequence and specifies the requested RAT capability information.

results.question: What is the final procedural step the initiating UE must perform after constructing the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message?
results.reference: The initiating UE must submit the constructed UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message to its lower layers for transmission.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.2.3, Actions related to transmission of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: The initiating UE shall submit the constructed UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message to lower layers for transmission to the target UE (i.e., over the sidelink/PC5 RRC path).
results.evidence: Most likely TS 38.331 clause 5.14.1.2, "Sidelink UE capability transfer – Initiation": after constructing UECapabilityEnquirySidelink, the initiating UE submits it to lower layers for transmission.

results.question: According to the clause, what specific characteristics define the delivery service that RRC expects from lower layers?
results.reference: The delivery service expected by RRC from lower layers is characterized as loss-less, in-sequence, and without duplication of information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 4.3.2, Services expected from lower layers
results.model_answer: RRC expects lower layers to provide an RRC-PDU delivery service that is reliable, preserves the transmission sequence, and does not deliver duplicates (i.e., effectively exactly-once, in-order delivery for the applicable signalling bearer).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2, "Services expected from lower layers". The clause characterizes the expected RRC-PDU delivery service as reliable, in-sequence, and without duplication.

results.question: How does the UE handle the buffer level values received from the upper layer when constructing the appLayerBufferLevelList?
results.reference: The UE sets the values in the list in order from newest to oldest received buffer level value, continuing until all received values are assigned or the configured maximum number of entries is reached.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.16.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE directly uses the buffer-level values supplied by upper layers to populate appLayerBufferLevelList: it includes the received values as the list entries (preserving their association/order with the configured application/service entries). RRC does not derive, average, or otherwise reinterpret them; the values must be representable by the ASN.1 range and the resulting list must satisfy the configured/ASN.1 list-size limits.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.3 (Application-layer measurement reporting; AppLayerMeasReport construction), together with the ASN.1 definition of AppLayerMeasReport/appLayerBufferLevelList and its element type. The procedure specifies use of buffer-level information obtained from upper layers when forming the application-layer buffer-level list.

results.question: What actions does the UE take if the encoded MeasurementReportAppLayer message exceeds the maximum PDCP SDU size and segmentation is allowed?
results.reference: The UE initiates the UL message segment transfer procedure as specified in clause 5.7.7, then submits the message to lower layers for transmission.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.16.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE segments the encoded MeasurementReportAppLayer into RRC-message segments sized so that each resulting PDCP SDU does not exceed the maximum PDCP SDU size. It sends the segments as ULDedicatedMessageSegment messages, carrying the successive portions of the original encoded message, with segment numbering and the appropriate non-final/final segment indication. The original oversized MeasurementReportAppLayer is therefore not sent as one PDCP SDU.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.7 (application-layer measurement reporting / MeasurementReportAppLayer transmission procedure), together with the ULDedicatedMessageSegment specification in clause 6.2.2. The procedure specifies use of ULDedicatedMessageSegment when the encoded MeasurementReportAppLayer exceeds the maximum PDCP SDU size and segmentation is allowed.

results.question: For a given measConfigAppLayerId, when does the UE include an application layer measurement report from the upper layers in the MeasurementReportAppLayer message?
results.reference: The UE includes it if the AS has received but not yet sent the report, and if application layer measurement reporting has not been suspended for that measConfigAppLayerId.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.16.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE includes an application-layer measurement report in a MeasurementReportAppLayer message when upper layers provide a report associated with the given measConfigAppLayerId and that ID corresponds to a currently configured (i.e., not released) MeasConfigAppLayer. The reporting is driven by receipt of the upper-layer report; it is not a normal RRC radio-measurement event/periodic trigger.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2, "Application layer measurement reporting" (subclause numbering is release-dependent). The procedure specifies that, upon receiving an application-layer measurement report from upper layers for a configured measConfigAppLayerId, the UE sends MeasurementReportAppLayer carrying that report.

results.question: How does the UE determine when to trigger an Event B2 measurement report according to the specified clause?
results.reference: The UE triggers Event B2 when the PCell's measurement quantity becomes worse than a configured threshold1 AND a neighbouring inter-RAT cell's measurement quantity becomes better than a configured threshold2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.9, Event B2 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and inter RAT neighbour becomes better than threshold2)
results.model_answer: The UE triggers an Event B2 report when both conditions are met for the configured timeToTrigger: (1) the serving-cell measurement is below threshold1, and (2) an inter-RAT neighbour measurement is above threshold2. The entering condition is: Ms + Hys < Thresh1 AND Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh2. After timeToTrigger expires, the UE sends the event-triggered measurement report (and may continue reporting per reportAmount/reportInterval).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.8 (Event B2): the entering condition is satisfied when "Ms + Hys < Thresh1" and "Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh2"; event triggering is subject to the configured timeToTrigger in the measurement reporting procedure.

results.question: What are the two distinct measurement conditions that must be simultaneously met for Event B2 to occur?
results.reference: Two conditions must be met: first, the serving PCell's quality falls below threshold1, and second, an inter-RAT neighbour cell's quality exceeds threshold2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.9, Event B2 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and inter RAT neighbour becomes better than threshold2)
results.model_answer: Event B2 is triggered only when both conditions are fulfilled simultaneously: (1) the serving PCell becomes worse than threshold1, and (2) the inter-RAT neighbour cell becomes better than threshold2. The conditions must remain satisfied for the configured timeToTrigger before reporting.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.8 (Event B2): "The UE shall consider that the entering condition for event B2 is met when the PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and the neighbour cell becomes better than threshold2."

results.question: How does the clause structure the triggering logic for Event B2 in terms of threshold comparisons?
results.reference: The triggering logic uses a dual-threshold comparison: one threshold (threshold1) for the worsening condition of the PCell, and a separate threshold (threshold2) for the improving condition of the inter-RAT neighbour.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.9, Event B2 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and inter RAT neighbour becomes better than threshold2)
results.model_answer: Event B2 is an AND-gated entry condition: the PCell/serving measurement must be worse than threshold1, while the inter-RAT neighbour measurement is better than threshold2. Formally, entry is when (Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Hys < Thresh1) AND (Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh2), subject to timeToTrigger. Thus, Thresh1 and Thresh2 are independently compared to serving and neighbour quantities; they are not compared directly to each other.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.10, "Event B2 (Inter-RAT)". It specifies the entering condition as: Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Hys < Thresh1 AND Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh2. It specifies leaving as: Mp + Ofp + Ocp - Hys > Thresh1 OR Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh2.

results.question: What action does the UE take to indicate the completion of the AS security activation procedure to the network?
results.reference: The UE indicates completion by sending an RRCReconfigurationComplete message, which is the first message that is both integrity protected and ciphered.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.4, Initial AS security activation
results.model_answer: The UE indicates completion of AS security activation by transmitting an RRC SecurityModeComplete message to the network (submitted to lower layers for transmission after applying the selected security configuration).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.4 (Security mode command): upon successful processing of a SecurityModeCommand, the UE submits a SecurityModeComplete message to lower layers for transmission; this signals completion of the AS security activation procedure.

results.question: How does the UE determine the content to include in the slrb-ConfigToReleaseList when constructing an RRCReconfigurationSidelink message?
results.reference: For each sidelink DRB that is to be released due to configuration by sl-ConfigDedicatedNR, SIB12, SidelinkPreconfigNR, or by upper layers, the UE sets the SLRB-PC5-ConfigIndex corresponding to that DRB in the slrb-ConfigToReleaseList.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1.2, Actions related to transmission of RRCReconfigurationSidelink message
results.model_answer: When initiating an RRCReconfigurationSidelink, the UE uses the upper-layer SLRB release request as the source of truth. It includes in slrb-ConfigToReleaseList the SLRB-Identity of each sidelink radio bearer that upper layers request to be released. The UE does not infer the list from other configured bearers; if no SLRB release is requested, the list is not included.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.1 (Sidelink RRC reconfiguration, UE initiation/transmission actions). The UE is instructed to include slrb-ConfigToReleaseList, when applicable, with the identities of the SLRBs for which it has received an upper-layer request to release the SLRB.

results.question: How does a UE in RRC_CONNECTED set the sl-MeasConfig in the RRCReconfigurationSidelink message for a frequency used for NR sidelink communication?
results.reference: If the frequency is included in sl-FreqInfoToAddModList in sl-ConfigDedicatedNR within an RRCReconfiguration message or in sl-ConfigCommonNR within SIB12, the UE sets the sl-MeasConfig according to the stored NR sidelink measurement configuration information for this destination.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1.2, Actions related to transmission of RRCReconfigurationSidelink message
results.model_answer: The UE copies the `sl-MeasConfig` that it received from the network in an `RRCReconfiguration` message for the NR sidelink frequency being used, and places that same configuration in the `RRCReconfigurationSidelink` message. Thus, in RRC_CONNECTED, the UE does not independently derive a new sidelink measurement configuration for that frequency; it forwards the network-provided `sl-MeasConfig` applicable to the used NR sidelink frequency.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3 (Sidelink RRC reconfiguration; exact subclause numbering is release-dependent): for a UE in RRC_CONNECTED, the UE shall set `sl-MeasConfig` in `RRCReconfigurationSidelink` to the `sl-MeasConfig` received in `RRCReconfiguration` for the frequency used for NR sidelink communication.

results.question: What actions does the UE take regarding PC5 Relay RLC channels when constructing the RRCReconfigurationSidelink message due to receiving sl-ConfigDedicatedNR?
results.reference: For each PC5 Relay RLC channel to be released, the UE sets the corresponding SL-RLC-ChannelConfig-PC5 in the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5. For each PC5 Relay RLC channel to be established or modified, the UE sets the SL-RLC-ChannelConfig-PC5 in the sl-RLC-ChannelToAddModList-PC5 according to the received sl-RLC-ChannelConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1.2, Actions related to transmission of RRCReconfigurationSidelink message
results.model_answer: On receipt of sl-ConfigDedicatedNR, a relay UE processes the PC5 Relay RLC-channel add/modify and release information when preparing RRCReconfigurationSidelink. It releases each PC5 Relay RLC channel explicitly indicated for release, and establishes a new channel or reconfigures an existing one for each add/modify entry, using the received RLC and logical-channel parameters. The UE includes the corresponding sidelink configuration in the RRCReconfigurationSidelink sent on PC5; channels not addressed by the received add/modify/release information are not implicitly recreated or removed.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, "UE actions upon reception of RRCReconfiguration"—the sl-ConfigDedicatedNR/relay-UE processing that requires construction of RRCReconfigurationSidelink and processing of PC5 Relay RLC-channel configuration, including add-or-modify and release handling. The exact ASN.1 field names and subclause numbering can vary by 38.331 release.

results.question: How should a UE in (NG)EN-DC behave if it is unable to comply with part of the configuration received in an RRCReconfiguration message over SRB3, and the message was received as part of ConditionalReconfiguration?
results.reference: The UE should continue using the configuration it was using prior to when the inability to comply was detected (or prior to the reception of the message). It does not apply any part of the new configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.8.2, Inability to comply with RRCReconfiguration
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate the conditional reconfiguration failure procedure. This is the specific handling for an RRCReconfiguration received via SRB3 when the UE cannot comply with all or part of a configuration that was received as part of ConditionalReconfiguration. It is not treated as the ordinary SRB3 reconfiguration-compliance case that would lead to the SCG failure information procedure. The UE does not complete the failed conditional configuration; the conditional-reconfiguration-failure procedure provides the applicable failure reporting, e.g. RRCReconfigurationFailure where configured/applicable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, "Reception of an RRCReconfiguration message" (the branch for inability to comply with configuration received via SRB3 and received as part of ConditionalReconfiguration). The clause directs the UE to initiate the conditional reconfiguration failure procedure. The detailed conditional-reconfiguration failure procedure is specified in the Conditional Reconfiguration subclauses of 5.3.5.

results.question: What actions are specified for a UE in (NG)EN-DC that is unable to comply with an RRCReconfiguration received over SRB3 (not part of ConditionalReconfiguration) when MCG transmission is not suspended?
results.reference: The UE shall initiate the SCG failure information procedure to report an SCG reconfiguration error, upon which the connection reconfiguration procedure ends.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.8.2, Inability to comply with RRCReconfiguration
results.model_answer: The UE shall perform the SCG failure information procedure and report failureType = scg-ReconfigFailure. It does not initiate RRC re-establishment under this stated condition (SRB3 reception and MCG transmission not suspended).
results.evidence: Most likely: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, "Actions upon reception of an RRCReconfiguration". The handling for inability to comply with an RRCReconfiguration received over SRB3, other than one associated with ConditionalReconfiguration, selects the SCG failure information procedure when MCG transmission is not suspended, with failure type set to scg-ReconfigFailure.

results.question: According to the clause, how does a UE handle fields in ServingCellConfigCommon that are defined in release-16 and later but that the UE does not support?
results.reference: The UE ignores such fields, meaning it does not take an action on them and does not store them. The specified UE behaviour in this clause does not apply to those fields.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.8.2, Inability to comply with RRCReconfiguration
results.model_answer: The UE shall ignore any ServingCellConfigCommon fields introduced in release 16 or a later release that it does not support. It does not apply configuration or behaviour based on such unsupported fields; supported fields remain processed normally.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, "Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE" (ServingCellConfigCommon handling): the UE is instructed to ignore fields in ServingCellConfigCommon that are specified for release 16 and later when those fields are not supported by the UE.

results.question: How does the mobility history information procedure specified in 5.7.9.1 apply to the different RRC states of the UE?
results.reference: The procedure covers how the UE stores mobility history information across all three RRC states: RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_CONNECTED.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.9.1, General
results.model_answer: The mobility-history procedure is primarily an RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE function: the UE maintains history of cells on which it camps while it is not RRC_CONNECTED. It is therefore intended to capture UE mobility that is not otherwise directly controlled by the network. In RRC_CONNECTED, mobility is handled by normal connected-mode mobility procedures (e.g., handover); the stored mobility history can be requested and reported to the network through the UE-information signalling, rather than being autonomously maintained/reported as a connected-mode mobility procedure.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.9.1, "Mobility history information - General". This clause defines UE maintenance of mobility-history information for RRC_IDLE and RRC_INACTIVE operation. Related signalling evidence is the mobility-history-report request/report information in the UEInformationRequest and UEInformationResponse procedures.

results.question: Across what scope of UE activity is the mobility history information storage procedure defined?
results.reference: The storage procedure is defined for UE activity encompassing the RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_CONNECTED states.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.9.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE mobility-history storage is defined to operate across all NR RRC states: RRC_CONNECTED, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_IDLE. It is therefore not limited to connected-mode mobility; it also covers mobility occurring through idle/inactive cell reselection.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3 (UE information procedure), mobility-history storage requirements. The relevant requirement states in substance that the UE stores mobility history information while in RRC_CONNECTED, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_IDLE.

results.question: Under what specific conditions must the UE trigger lower layers to initiate a measurement gap activation request using UL MAC CE?
results.reference: The UE must trigger this request when: 1) upper layers indicate to start performing location measurements towards E-UTRA or NR or start subframe and slot timing detection towards E-UTRA, 2) the UE requires measurement gaps for these operations while gaps are either not configured or not sufficient, and 3) preconfigured measurement gaps are configured and the UE considers at least one meets the measurement gap requirements.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.6.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE shall trigger lower layers to send a Measurement Gap Activation Request UL MAC CE when it has an RRC-configured measurement-gap configuration for a gap that is subject to MAC-controlled activation, and the UE needs that gap to perform a configured measurement. In particular, the request is made when the relevant configured measurement requires a gap (for example, an inter-frequency/inter-RAT measurement that cannot be performed without a gap) and that measurement gap is not already activated. Receipt of MeasConfig alone does not by itself imply an activation request; there must be an actual configured measurement need for the MAC-controlled gap.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.2 (Measurement gap configuration / UE measurement-gap behaviour; clause title and subclause numbering can vary by release). The normative UE procedure states that, for a configured measurement-gap configuration supporting activation, the UE triggers lower layers to initiate a measurement-gap activation request using UL MAC CE when the UE needs the measurement gap for measurements. The corresponding UL MAC CE format/procedure is specified in TS 38.321 (UL-SCH MAC CE for measurement-gap activation request).

results.question: When must the UE initiate the procedure to indicate stop of location measurements or timing detection?
results.reference: The UE must initiate the stop procedure if and only if upper layers indicate to stop performing location measurements towards E-UTRA or NR or stop subframe and slot timing detection towards E-UTRA, and preConfigGapID is not activated.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.6.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate the LocationMeasurementIndication procedure to report stop when lower layers indicate that the UE has stopped performing the requested location measurements or timing detection (normally after it had indicated their start). This is a stop-status indication; it is not triggered merely by an arbitrary UE decision or by a generic RRC measurement-report event.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.6.14, "Location measurement indication" (UE actions / procedure initiation). The clause specifies that the UE initiates the procedure to indicate stop of location measurements or timing detection upon an indication from lower layers that those activities have stopped.

results.question: How does the procedure initiation differ for a UE capable of NR sidelink discovery?
results.reference: A UE capable of NR sidelink discovery may initiate the procedure to indicate its interest in receiving or transmitting NR sidelink discovery, triggered by the same general cases as for communication (e.g., connection establishment, change of interest). Specifically for discovery, it may initiate to request assignment of dedicated resources for sidelink discovery transmission or sidelink discovery reception.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: NR sidelink-discovery capability does not by itself autonomously start an RRC procedure. The UE initiates the Sidelink UE Information procedure when upper layers provide or change discovery-related requirements (e.g., a request for discovery transmission resources or discovery-reception interest). It then reports the applicable discovery information to the serving gNB. This differs from the communication case only in the trigger/report content: sidelink communication uses communication TX/RX interest and destination information, whereas discovery uses discovery TX-resource request and/or discovery RX-interest information. If the UE is not RRC_CONNECTED, any needed establishment/resume is governed by the normal RRC connection-control rules; discovery capability is not a separate RRC establishment cause.
results.evidence: Most likely: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.10.6.1, "Sidelink UE Information" — Initiation (clause numbering may vary by release). It specifies UE initiation of the sidelink-information reporting procedure based on upper-layer sidelink information, including NR sidelink discovery transmission-resource requests and discovery reception-interest information. Related connection establishment/resume behavior is specified in the RRC connection-control initiation clauses, rather than as a distinct discovery-specific establishment procedure.

results.question: How does the network inform UEs about changes to MCCH information, and what is the timing of these notifications?
results.reference: The network notifies UEs about MCCH information changes via PDCCH scheduling the MCCH in every repetition period within the current modification period.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.1.3, MCCH information validity and notification of changes
results.model_answer: The network announces an upcoming MCCH update by sending an MCCH-change notification on PDCCH using the MBS/MCCH notification RNTI configured for the service area. A UE that detects the notification acquires the MCCH according to the broadcast MCCH configuration. The notification is sent in the configured notification occasions (derived from the broadcast notification timing configuration) during the modification period preceding the changed MCCH. The changed MCCH becomes applicable at the next MCCH modification-period boundary; it is not changed arbitrarily within an ongoing modification period.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.1 (MBS reception, including MCCH acquisition/change-notification behaviour), together with the MBS broadcast/MCCH configuration IEs in the SystemInformation definitions. The normative principle is that MCCH changes are announced by a PDCCH notification and take effect at an MCCH modification-period boundary.

results.question: What does the MSB in the 2-bit bitmap notification indicate when set to '1', and what does the LSB indicate when set to '1'?
results.reference: The MSB set to '1' indicates the start of MBS service(s). The LSB set to '1' indicates modification of MCCH information other than changes caused by new MBS service start, such as configuration modification of ongoing sessions, session stop, or neighbouring cell information modification.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.1.3, MCCH information validity and notification of changes
results.model_answer: When set to '1', the MSB indicates a system-information modification notification. When set to '1', the LSB indicates an ETWS and/or CMAS notification.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.5.2 (Paging) and the ShortMessage IE definition: ShortMessage is a 2-bit bitmap with bit meanings systemInfoModification (MSB) and etwsAndCmasIndication (LSB).

results.question: When can changes to MCCH information occur, and how is the transmission of unchanged information handled within a modification period?
results.reference: Changes to MCCH information only occur at specific radio frames using a modification period concept. Within a modification period, the same MCCH information may be transmitted multiple times according to its scheduling based on a repetition period.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.1.3, MCCH information validity and notification of changes
results.model_answer: MCCH information may change only at the boundary/start of an MCCH modification period. It is stable for the whole modification period. Consequently, transmissions in later MCCH repetition occasions within that period carry the same (unchanged) MCCH information; the UE keeps using it until a subsequent modification-period boundary introduces a new version.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, MBS/MCCH procedures, clause titled "MCCH information" (wording defining the MCCH modification period and MCCH repetition period). The clause states in substance that MCCH information can be changed only at the beginning of a modification period and is transmitted periodically according to the configured repetition period.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the paging procedure as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to transmit paging information to a UE that is in either the RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The paging procedure primarily enables the network to deliver paging information to a UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE, notably to trigger RRC connection establishment or RRC connection resume (and, where applicable, to notify the UE of system-information or public-warning updates).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3 (Paging): the paging procedure is defined as being used to transfer paging information to a UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE; its listed uses include initiating RRC connection establishment, initiating RRC connection resume, and notifying relevant system-information/public-warning changes.

results.question: How does the paging procedure initiate communication with a UE according to the clause?
results.reference: It initiates communication by transmitting paging information specifically to a UE operating in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The network initiates communication through paging by transmitting a Paging message (on PCCH) addressed to the UE's paging identity. A UE that detects a matching paging record uses the indicated purpose to initiate the applicable access procedure, typically RRC connection establishment from RRC_IDLE or RRC resume from RRC_INACTIVE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.1 (Paging — General): "The network initiates the paging procedure by transmitting the Paging message."

results.question: To which RRC states does the paging procedure apply based on the provided clause?
results.reference: The procedure applies when the UE is in the RRC_IDLE state or the RRC_INACTIVE state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The paging procedure applies to UEs in RRC_IDLE and RRC_INACTIVE for connection establishment/resume and system-information-change notification. It also applies to RRC_CONNECTED for ETWS/CMAS warning indications.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.1 (Paging—General): the Paging message is used to initiate RRC connection establishment/resume for idle/inactive UEs, to notify RRC_IDLE and RRC_INACTIVE UEs of system-information modification, and to inform RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE and RRC_CONNECTED UEs of ETWS/CMAS indications.

results.question: Why is the paging procedure necessary for UEs in specific RRC states?
results.reference: It is necessary to deliver paging information to UEs that are not in a connected state (RRC_CONNECTED), specifically those in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE, to alert them or initiate downlink communication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.2.1, General
results.model_answer: Paging is necessary because a UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE has no continuously active dedicated radio connection and therefore does not continuously monitor downlink scheduling. The network uses paging at UE-specific Paging Occasions to preserve UE battery and radio resources while retaining downlink reachability. A paging indication can cause an RRC_IDLE UE to establish an RRC connection, or an RRC_INACTIVE UE to resume its stored RRC/AS context. Paging also notifies such UEs of relevant system-information modification and public-warning indications. RRC_CONNECTED UEs are normally reached through dedicated control/data signaling rather than the idle/inactive paging procedure.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.1, "General" (Paging). This clause defines paging for UEs in RRC_IDLE and RRC_INACTIVE, including triggering RRC connection establishment or RRC resume and conveying system-information/public-warning related indications.

results.question: How does the broadcast MRB configuration procedure enable a UE to receive an MBS broadcast service?
results.reference: The procedure configures the PDCP, RLC, MAC, and physical layer entities in the UE, which is necessary to start receiving the broadcast MRB transmitted on the MTCH.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The network broadcasts an MBSBroadcastConfiguration for an advertised MBS broadcast service. After acquiring the relevant MBS session information, the UE selects the applicable configuration and configures the indicated MRB and its associated lower-layer reception parameters (e.g., bearer identity/mapping and radio/MAC-RLC-PDCP-related configuration). The UE can then monitor the configured MBS transmission resources/control information and receive the broadcast data on that MRB. Because this is broadcast reception, the configuration is common rather than UE-specific and does not require a UE acknowledgement or RRC reconfiguration completion.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3, "Broadcast MRB configuration" (clause numbering can vary slightly by TS 38.331 release/version). This procedure specifies UE handling of broadcast MRB configuration for MBS service reception.

results.question: What is the purpose of the broadcast MRB configuration procedure when a UE stops receiving a broadcast service?
results.reference: The procedure is used to configure the UE's protocol layers (PDCP, RLC, MAC, physical) upon stopping reception of a broadcast MRB, likely to deconfigure or release relevant resources.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.3.1, General
results.model_answer: When the UE stops receiving a broadcast service, the broadcast MRB configuration procedure is used to release/deconfigure the MRB(s) associated with that service. This stops the corresponding MBS user-plane reception and frees the UE’s radio-protocol resources; it is not, by itself, an RRC connection release or necessarily a network notification.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause titled "Broadcast MRB configuration" (within the MBS procedures; clause numbering may differ by release). The UE behavior specifies releasing the MRB associated with an MBS broadcast service when the UE stops receiving that service.

results.question: How does the UE evaluate when the leaving condition for Event S1 is triggered?
results.reference: The UE evaluates that the leaving condition is triggered upon the fulfillment of condition S1-2, as defined in the specification.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.4.2, Event S1 (Serving becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: For Event S1, the UE considers the leaving condition fulfilled when Ms + Hys < Thresh. Ms is the applicable S1 measurement result, Hys is the configured hysteresis, and Thresh is the Event-S1 threshold. Thus, after S1 has entered, the measured value must fall below the threshold by the hysteresis margin; equality does not satisfy the strict '<' leaving condition. The condition is subject to the configured timeToTrigger before a leaving-triggered report/action is generated, where applicable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause covering Event-triggered sidelink measurement reporting / Event S1 definition (release-dependent clause numbering, commonly under the sidelink measurement-reporting procedure). The Event S1 leaving expression is specified as: S1-2: Ms + Hys < Thresh.

results.question: In the current release of the specification, for which two specific UL DCCH messages is segmentation applicable?
results.reference: Segmentation is only applicable to UECapabilityInformation and MeasurementReportAppLayer messages.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.7.1, General ULDedicatedMessageSegment
results.model_answer: Segmentation is applicable only to the UL DCCH messages UECapabilityInformation and ULInformationTransferMRDC.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3 (RRC message segmentation), especially its general/procedure text restricting UL RRC message segmentation to UECapabilityInformation and ULInformationTransferMRDC. The associated ASN.1 support is UL-DedicatedMessageSegment-r16 in the UL-DCCH message definitions of clause 6.2.2.

results.question: How does the clause specify the state of the UE when the UL dedicated message segmentation procedure is used?
results.reference: The UE must be in the RRC_CONNECTED state for this procedure to be used.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.7.1, General ULDedicatedMessageSegment
results.model_answer: The procedure is specified for use only while the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED. It is not applicable in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.4 (UL dedicated message segmentation): "The UE shall use the UL dedicated message segmentation procedure only in RRC_CONNECTED state."

results.question: How does the UE determine which measurements to perform when it is in RRC_CONNECTED state?
results.reference: The UE performs measurements based on the measurement configuration provided by the network in the RRCConnectionReconfiguration message or the measurement configuration received in the RRCResume message, as per the stored configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.3, Performing measurements
results.model_answer: In RRC_CONNECTED, the UE determines what to measure from the network-provided MeasConfig. The UE applies each configured measurement object (e.g., NR/UTRA/E-UTRA frequencies/cells, SSB or CSI-RS resources and associated cell lists), measurement quantity configuration, and measurement gap/SMTC-related settings. A measId links a measurement object to a reporting configuration; this determines the event- or periodical-reporting criteria for measurements. Thus, the UE performs the measurements required by the configured measurement objects and reports results only according to the associated report configurations and measIds.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration): the network configures UE measurements using MeasConfig; measurement objects define what is measured, report configurations define reporting criteria, and measurement identities associate a measurement object with a report configuration. See also clauses 5.5.2.1 (MeasConfig), 5.5.2.2 (Measurement objects), 5.5.2.3 (Report configurations), and 5.5.2.4 (Measurement identities).

results.question: Why might a UE in RRC_INACTIVE state perform measurements?
results.reference: A UE in RRC_INACTIVE state performs measurements if it has a stored measurement configuration and the resumption of suspended measurements is triggered, for example, upon cell reselection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.3, Performing measurements
results.model_answer: An RRC_INACTIVE UE measures radio cells primarily to support autonomous cell selection/reselection while retaining its suspended AS context. Reselection lets it remain on a suitable cell as radio conditions or priorities change. If the newly selected cell is outside the configured RAN Notification Area (RNA), the UE performs an RNA update so the network can continue to page it. These are local mobility measurements, not necessarily RRC_CONNECTED-style measurement reports. The UE may also perform configured logged measurements for network/MDT optimization.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.2 (RRC_INACTIVE), which specifies that an RRC_INACTIVE UE performs cell selection/reselection, monitors paging, and performs RAN notification area updates. Cell-selection/reselection measurement/ranking behavior is specified in TS 38.304 and uses reselection-related information delivered by RRC/system information.

results.question: What is the primary limitation on UE requirements regarding the contents of the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message?
results.reference: UE requirements related to the contents of the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message are limited to those explicitly specified elsewhere, such as in the corresponding field descriptions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2.4, Actions upon reception of the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message
results.model_answer: The UE is only required to support an MBSBroadcastConfiguration that contains configuration for a single MBS frequency. It is not required to support a message carrying MBS configuration for multiple frequencies.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, MBS broadcast-configuration acquisition/procedure text associated with MBSBroadcastConfiguration (clause 5.8, Release-17 MBS procedures): the UE is not required to support an MBSBroadcastConfiguration containing more than one MBS frequency configuration.

results.question: What is the scope of UE actions defined for handling the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message?
results.reference: The clause does not define independent UE requirements for the message contents; it defers to requirements specified elsewhere, such as in field descriptions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2.4, Actions upon reception of the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message
results.model_answer: The MBSBroadcastConfiguration handling is scoped to broadcast MBS reception configuration. It is not an RRC reconfiguration procedure for a particular UE: receipt of the message does not itself cause an RRC state transition, security change, SRB/DRB setup, or modification of unicast radio resources. The UE uses the broadcast information, where applicable, to support reception/monitoring of the advertised MBS configuration; any further MBS-session or radio-bearer actions are governed by the corresponding MBS/session procedures and configuration information.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.1.2 (MBSBroadcastConfiguration, including its General/UE-behaviour subclause where present in the applicable release). This clause defines the MBS broadcast-configuration message and its MBS-reception purpose; it is distinct from the UE-specific RRC reconfiguration procedures in clause 5.3.5 (RRCReconfiguration).

results.question: Upon reception of RRCReject, which specific clause's actions are mandated for the UE?
results.reference: The UE is required to carry out the actions detailed in clause 5.3.15.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.5, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall perform the actions specified in TS 38.331 clause 5.3.3.5, “RRC connection establishment failure.”
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.5 is the normative RRC connection-establishment-failure procedure invoked on reception of RRCReject during RRC establishment.

results.question: What is the UE's obligation following the reception of an RRCReject message?
results.reference: The UE must perform the actions as specified in clause 5.3.15 of the specification.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.5, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: On reception of RRCReject, the UE shall stop T300, enter RRC_IDLE, and perform cell selection (using redirectedCarrierInfo when provided). If waitTime is included, the UE shall start T302 with that value; while T302 is running, a new RRC establishment attempt is barred subject to the procedure’s specified exceptions/conditions.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.4, "Reception of an RRCReject by the UE": specifies stopping T300, starting T302 when waitTime is present, performing cell selection (including redirection where indicated), and entering RRC_IDLE.

results.question: How does the UE handle the removal of a measObjectId when there are associated measurement identities (measIds) configured?
results.reference: The UE removes all measIds associated with that measObjectId from the measIdList, and for each removed measId, it also removes the corresponding reporting entry from VarMeasReportList and stops/resets any running relevant timer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.4, Measurement object removal
results.model_answer: Removing a measObjectId removes only the corresponding measurement object. The UE does not implicitly delete measIds that reference that measObjectId; those measIds must be explicitly removed via measIdToRemoveList if the network intends to delete them. After the measurement object is removed, an associated measId is not considered configured because its referenced measObject is no longer configured, and the UE cannot use it for measurement reporting until a valid associated measObject is configured again.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.2 (Measurement configuration / MeasConfig): the UE processes measObjectToRemoveList by removing the identified measurement object(s), and processes measIdToRemoveList separately by removing the identified measurement identity/identities. The same clause specifies that a measId is considered configured only when its associated measurement object and report configuration are configured.

results.question: How should the UE treat a measObjectToRemoveList that includes a measObjectId value not currently configured in the UE?
results.reference: The UE does not consider the message as erroneous; it simply ignores such non-configured measObjectId values as per the note in the specification.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.4, Measurement object removal
results.model_answer: The UE should ignore that measObjectId: removal has no effect when no currently configured measurement object matches the listed ID. It shall not treat this as an RRC configuration failure or remove any other measurement object.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration), UE processing of MeasConfig. For each measObjectId in measObjectToRemoveList, the UE removes the measurement object with the matching measObjectId; consequently, an ID for which no object is configured has no matching object and results in no action. The corresponding ASN.1 container is MeasConfig.measObjectToRemoveList in clause 6.3.2.

results.question: How does the network provide configuration parameters for each connected L2 U2N Remote UE?
results.reference: The network provides configuration parameters for each connected L2 U2N Remote UE that is indicated in the sl-L2Identity-Remote list.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15.1, General
results.model_answer: The gNB configures each connected L2 U2N Remote UE by sending an RRCReconfiguration to the L2 U2N Relay UE. The message carries an SL-L2U2N-RemoteUE-Config-r17 (or the applicable later-release extension) for the identified Remote UE; the relay uses that per-Remote-UE configuration for the L2 U2N relay operation.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.3.2 (RRCReconfiguration and IE definitions), specifically the SL-L2U2N-RemoteUE-Config-r17 IE and its use in RRCReconfiguration. The procedural sidelink/L2 U2N relay text in clause 5.7 is the complementary evidence.

results.question: What action does the UE take if the received sl-L2RelayUEConfig contains the sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList?
results.reference: The UE performs the L2 U2N Remote UE release procedure as specified in section 5.3.5.15.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15.1, General
results.model_answer: For each remote-UE identity in sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList, the UE releases the corresponding L2-relay remote-UE context, including the associated sidelink RLC bearer(s)/configuration maintained for that remote UE.
results.evidence: Most likely: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (RRCReconfiguration procedure; processing of sl-L2RelayUEConfig), in the sidelink L2 relay UE configuration handling text. The sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList is interpreted as removal of the identified remote-UE configuration and its associated SL radio-bearer state.

results.question: What triggers the UE to perform L2 U2N Remote UE addition or modification?
results.reference: The UE performs L2 U2N Remote UE addition or modification when the received sl-L2RelayUEConfig contains the sl-RemoteUE-ToAddModList.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE (acting as an L2 U2N relay) performs L2 U2N Remote UE addition or modification when it receives an RRCReconfiguration containing L2 U2N Remote-UE configuration for a remote UE (i.e., the applicable L2U2N/RemoteUE configuration IE or add/modify entry). The RRC-provided configuration, not PC5 discovery by itself, is the trigger.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (RRCReconfiguration procedure, especially the UE actions on reception of RRCReconfiguration and the L2 U2N Remote UE addition/modification sub-procedure). The relevant normative condition is the presence of the L2 U2N Remote UE configuration in RRCReconfiguration; exact subclause numbering can vary by 38.331 release/version.

results.question: What is the purpose of the network configuring the L2 U2N Relay UE with relay operation related configurations?
results.reference: The network configures the L2 U2N Relay UE with relay operation related configurations to manage connections with L2 U2N Remote UEs, including providing parameters and triggering release or addition/modification procedures.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15.1, General
results.model_answer: The purpose is to authorize and enable the UE to act as an L2 U2N Relay UE, i.e., to forward traffic between remote UE(s) over PC5 and the network over Uu. The relay-operation configuration provides the radio/bearer and relay-service parameters needed for that forwarding operation, including the applicable sidelink/relay bearer configuration and associated relay-service context.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3 (Sidelink configuration), specifically the RRCReconfiguration processing for L2 U2N relay configuration (e.g., sl-RelayUE-Config-r17). The procedure states the network configures the UE with relay-operation-related configuration for operation as an L2 U2N Relay UE.

results.question: How does the UE handle the release of RLC bearers when configured via CellGroupConfig?
results.reference: If the CellGroupConfig contains rlc-BearerToReleaseList or rlc-BearerToReleaseListExt, the UE performs RLC bearer release as specified in 5.3.5.5.3.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.1, General
results.model_answer: {'handling': 'When the UE applies a CellGroupConfig, it processes rlc-BearerToReleaseList as an explicit delta. For each listed logicalChannelIdentity, the UE releases the corresponding RLC bearer/RLC entity in that cell group and removes its associated MAC logical-channel configuration. The released RLC entity stops operating and its RLC state/buffers are disposed of according to RLC procedures.', 'scope': 'This is an RLC/MAC logical-channel release, not automatically a release of the complete PDCP/SDAP radio bearer. Release of a DRB (and its PDCP entity) is controlled separately by RadioBearerConfig, e.g. drb-ToReleaseList. A bearer is not implicitly released merely because it is absent from rlc-BearerToAddModList; it must be identified in rlc-BearerToReleaseList or released through another applicable procedure.', 'reasoning': 'CellGroupConfig uses list-based add/modify and release semantics. The release-list key is logicalChannelIdentity, which identifies the RLC bearer and its MAC logical channel within the configured cell group.'}
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (UE reception/processing of RRCReconfiguration, including application of CellGroupConfig), read with clause 6.3.2 definitions of CellGroupConfig and RLC-BearerConfig. In particular, CellGroupConfig contains rlc-BearerToReleaseList, whose entries are logicalChannelIdentity values identifying RLC bearers to be released. Exact subclause numbering can vary slightly by TS 38.331 release/version.

results.question: How does the UE process the addition or modification of SCells based on the received CellGroupConfig?
results.reference: If the CellGroupConfig contains sCellToAddModList, the UE performs SCell addition/modification as specified in 5.3.5.5.9.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE examines CellGroupConfig.sCellToAddModList. For each SCellConfig, it uses sCellIndex as the identity: if that index does not correspond to an already configured SCell, the UE adds/configures the SCell; if it is already configured, the UE modifies that SCell according to the received SCellConfig. Absence of sCellToAddModList means no SCell add/modify action. SCell configuration is distinct from SCell activation/deactivation, which follows the applicable SCell-state procedures.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.2, "Cell group configuration" (most likely evidence clause): the UE processes CellGroupConfig.sCellToAddModList and, for each SCellConfig, adds an SCell when its sCellIndex is not configured and modifies it when that sCellIndex is already configured.

results.question: What specific action must the UE take if upper layers indicate barring of the PCell during initiation?
results.reference: The UE shall treat the PCell used prior to entering RRC_IDLE as barred according to TS 38.304.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.9.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE shall consider the RRC re-establishment procedure to have failed. It then applies the specified RRC re-establishment failure handling (including transition toward RRC_IDLE/cell selection as applicable).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.2.2 (RRC re-establishment — Initiation): if upper layers indicate that the PCell is barred, the UE shall consider the RRC re-establishment procedure to have failed.

results.question: Describe the procedure for removing a sidelink measurement identity when it is listed in sl-MeasIdToRemoveList and is present in the UE's VarMeasConfigSL.
results.reference: The procedure involves two removal steps: deleting the identity from the sl-MeasIdList in the VarMeasConfigSL, and deleting the NR sidelink measurement reporting entry for that identity from the VarMeasReportListSL, provided such a reporting entry exists.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.2, Sidelink measurement identity removal
results.model_answer: For each sidelink measurement identity in sl-MeasIdToRemoveList, if that sl-MeasId exists in the UE's VarMeasConfigSL, the UE removes the corresponding entry from VarMeasConfigSL.sl-MeasIdList. This removes the association between the sidelink measurement object and sidelink report configuration represented by that identity. It does not, by this action alone, remove the referenced sidelink measurement object or report configuration; those are removed only when explicitly indicated by their respective removal lists.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.1 (Measurement configuration), sidelink measurement-configuration processing for sl-MeasConfig: processing of sl-MeasIdToRemoveList requires removal of the matching sidelink measurement identity from the UE variable VarMeasConfigSL.

results.question: How does a UE determine the sorting quantity for beam measurement information when reportType is set to eventTriggered?
results.reference: The UE uses a priority-based fallback chain: first the trigger quantity if available, otherwise RSRP if available, otherwise RSRQ if available, otherwise SINR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.2, Reporting of beam measurement information
results.model_answer: For an eventTriggered ReportConfigNR, the UE sorts reported beam/RS-index measurement information in descending order using reportQuantityRS-Indexes. If reportQuantityRS-Indexes is sameAsCell, the sorting quantity is reportQuantityCell. If reportQuantityRS-Indexes explicitly selects rsrp, rsrq, or sinr, that selected quantity is used. If the RS-index quantity is not configured, the applicable default sorting quantity is RSRP. The event trigger metric itself does not override an explicitly configured RS-index reporting quantity.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, most likely clause 5.5.3, Measurement reporting (including beam/RS-index measurement-result reporting rules), together with the ReportConfigNR ASN.1 definitions for reportQuantityCell and reportQuantityRS-Indexes.

results.question: For periodical reporting with a single reporting quantity set to true in reportQuantityRS-Indexes, how is the sorting quantity determined?
results.reference: The UE considers the configured single quantity as the sorting quantity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.2, Reporting of beam measurement information
results.model_answer: With exactly one reportQuantityRS-Indexes field set to true, that field's corresponding RS-index measurement quantity is the sorting quantity. The UE ranks the reported RS indexes in descending order of that quantity (e.g., ssb-Index-RSRP selects SS-RSRP; csi-RS-Index-SINR selects CSI-RS-SINR). No multi-quantity priority/selection rule is needed in this case.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.5.3 (Periodical reporting), in the RS-index reporting/sorting requirements associated with reportQuantityRS-Indexes; see also the ReportConfigNR IE definition in clause 6.3.2.

results.question: When including SS/PBCH block based beam measurement information, which beams are included in resultsSSB-Indexes?
results.reference: The index associated with the best beam for that SS/PBCH block sorting quantity is always included. Additionally, if absThreshSS-BlocksConsolidation is configured for the associated measObject, any remaining beams whose sorting quantity is above that threshold are also included.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.2, Reporting of beam measurement information
results.model_answer: resultsSSB-Indexes contains the measurement results for the best N SS/PBCH-block beams of the reported NR cell, where N is configured by maxNrofRS-IndexesToReport. “Best” is determined using the configured RS-index reporting quantity (e.g., SS-RSRP, SS-RSRQ, or SS-SINR); the reported entries identify the corresponding SSB indexes and include the configured measurement quantities.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.3.2 (measurement reporting), together with the ReportConfigNR definition: when beam measurements are included for SS/PBCH-block-based measurements, the UE reports resultsSSB-Indexes for the best N SS/PBCH blocks, with N determined by maxNrofRS-IndexesToReport.

results.question: Under what condition does the UE include detailed measurement results for each SS/PBCH block index in the beam measurement report?
results.reference: Detailed SS/PBCH based measurement results for the quantities in reportQuantityRS-Indexes are included for each SS/PBCH block index when includeBeamMeasurements is set to true.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.2, Reporting of beam measurement information
results.model_answer: The UE includes per-SS/PBCH-block (SSB) measurement details when the applicable ReportConfigNR configures reportQuantityRS-Indexes for an SSB-index quantity (ssb-Index-RSRP, ssb-Index-RSRQ, or ssb-Index-SINR). The UE then reports the configured quantity for the reportable SSB indexes, limited by maxNrofRS-IndexesToReport and subject to the configured SSB selection/threshold rules (for example, ssb-RSRP-Threshold where applicable).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.3.1 (Measurement reporting—general): RS-index/beam-level results are included when reportQuantityRS-Indexes is configured. For SSB reporting, the configured SSB-index report quantity causes the UE to include SS/PBCH block index results; the number of reported indexes is governed by maxNrofRS-IndexesToReport. Relevant ASN.1 is ReportConfigNR.reportQuantityRS-Indexes and MeasResultCellNR.measResultRS-IndexList.

results.question: What is the purpose of the SCGFailureInformation procedure in 3GPP TS 38.331?
results.reference: The procedure informs the E-UTRAN or NR Master Node (MN) about a Secondary Cell Group (SCG) failure that the UE has experienced.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3.1, General RRC reconfiguration SCGFailureInformation
results.model_answer: The SCGFailureInformation procedure enables a UE in dual connectivity to report a detected Secondary Cell Group (SCG) failure to the Master Node (MN), normally via the MCG RRC connection. It provides the MN with the SCG failure cause and, where applicable, SCG measurements, so that the MN can decide recovery actions such as SCG reconfiguration, SCG release, or other RRC reconfiguration. The procedure is a failure-reporting mechanism; it does not by itself restore the SCG.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.2 (SCG failure information), especially clause 5.7.2.1 "General", which states in substance that the SCG failure information procedure is used to report SCG failure to the MN.

results.question: What specific type of SCG failure related to synchronization reconfiguration does the SCGFailureInformation procedure report?
results.reference: It reports a failure of SCG reconfiguration with sync.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3.1, General RRC reconfiguration SCGFailureInformation
results.model_answer: It reports the failure type `scg-ReconfigFailure`: an SCG failure caused by failure to execute an SCG reconfiguration with synchronization (`reconfigurationWithSync`), rather than a generic radio-link or RLC failure.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.2.5 (UL-DCCH message `SCGFailureInformation`) together with the `SCGFailureInformationIEs` definition in clause 6.3.2. The `failureType` enumeration includes `scg-ReconfigFailure`; the SCG reconfiguration-with-sync procedure specifies reporting this type when that synchronization reconfiguration fails.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the access barring check procedure described in the clause?
results.reference: The procedure performs an access barring check for an access attempt associated with a given Access Category and one or more Access Identities, upon request from upper layers or the RRC layer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14.1, General
results.model_answer: The access barring check determines whether a UE is allowed to initiate a requested access attempt at that time. It applies configured barring information (for example, access category/identity and barring factors/timers); if the attempt is barred, the UE defers the attempt until the applicable barring time expires. Its primary purpose is therefore to control and limit UE access attempts, particularly during congestion or overload, while allowing prioritized/emergency access as configured.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.14 (Access barring): the UE performs an access barring check before an access attempt and, when the check indicates barring, does not initiate the access attempt and applies the associated barring time. The procedure uses broadcast access-barring configuration, including UAC/AC barring information where applicable.

results.question: Under what condition must a UE in RRC_CONNECTED defer access barring checks after a PCell change?
results.reference: The UE must defer access barring checks until it has obtained SIB1 from the target cell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14.1, General
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED defers access-barring checks when it is executing an RRCReconfiguration that changes the PCell—i.e., the reconfiguration contains reconfigurationWithSync for the PCell. The deferral applies while the PCell-change/mobility reconfiguration is ongoing, until that procedure completes or fails; access barring must not interrupt the commanded move to the target PCell.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.2, “Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE” (the reconfigurationWithSync/PCell-change handling). The associated UE behaviour specifies deferral of access-barring checking during an ongoing PCell-change reconfiguration. Exact subclause numbering/text can vary by TS 38.331 release.

results.question: Which two types of entities are explicitly excluded from applying this access barring check procedure?
results.reference: The procedure does not apply to IAB-MT, nor to an L2 U2N Relay UE initiating RRC connection establishment or resume upon receiving a message from a remote UE via SL-RLC0 or SL-RLC1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14.1, General
results.model_answer: The access-barring check is explicitly not applied by (1) a UE requesting emergency services and (2) a UE performing high-priority access (e.g., access associated with priority service handling).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.14 (Access control), in the access-barring-check procedure: the procedure excludes emergency-service access and high-priority access from access barring.

results.question: From which sources can a request to perform this access barring check originate?
results.reference: A request can originate from upper layers according to TS 24.501 or from the RRC layer itself.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14.1, General
results.model_answer: A request to run the UE access-barring (Unified Access Control) check can originate from either NAS (an upper-layer access request) or AS/RRC (an access-stratum-originated request). Broadcast system information only supplies the barring configuration; it is not itself the requester.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.14.2 (Unified access control procedure / access barring check). The procedure distinguishes requests originating from NAS and from AS, with the UE using the applicable access category/identity and the UAC barring information broadcast by the cell.

results.question: How does the UE determine when to perform measurements on a serving cell?
results.reference: The UE performs measurements on the serving cell based on the measurement configuration provided by the network, which includes measurement objects, reporting configurations, and measurement identities that link them. The UE measures quantities like RSRP and RSRQ according to the parameters in the relevant measurement object.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5, Measurements
results.model_answer: In RRC_CONNECTED, the UE does not autonomously choose arbitrary serving-cell measurement times. It performs serving-cell measurements when required by the received MeasConfig/measId, using the configured measurement reference signals and their timing: SSB measurements follow the applicable SSB Measurement Timing Configuration (SMTC), and CSI-RS measurements follow the configured CSI-RS resources/periodicity. The resulting measurements are evaluated against the linked reportConfig (for example A1/A2 serving-cell events, relative events, or periodic reporting); event reporting occurs only after the configured trigger condition and timeToTrigger are satisfied. Measurement gaps may enable measurements that cannot otherwise be scheduled, but do not themselves define the serving-cell measurement/reporting criterion. In RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE, serving-cell and reselection measurements follow the cell-reselection measurement rules/configuration (principally TS 38.304 and broadcast RRC information), rather than connected-mode MeasConfig.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.1 (Measurement configuration—General), together with clauses 5.5.2.3 (Measurement objects), 5.5.2.4 (Reporting configurations), and 5.5.4 (Measurement reporting). These specify that the UE applies the network-provided measurement configuration; MeasObjectNR provides SSB/CSI-RS measurement configuration and applicable SMTC behavior, while ReportConfigNR defines event/periodical reporting and timeToTrigger. Relevant event definitions include serving-cell events A1 and A2.

results.question: How does the network control the reporting of measurement results by the UE?
results.reference: The network controls reporting through reporting configurations, which define criteria like event-triggered or periodic reporting, along with associated parameters such as hysteresis and time-to-trigger. The UE reports when the linked measurement identity conditions are satisfied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5, Measurements
results.model_answer: The network controls UE measurement-result reporting through the MeasConfig delivered in RRCReconfiguration. It configures measurement objects (what to measure), report configurations (when/how to report), and measId associations (which object uses which reporting rule). ReportConfigNR can select periodic or event-triggered reporting and control event thresholds, hysteresis, time-to-trigger, report-on-leave, report interval, report amount, reported quantities, and maximum cells/RS indexes. The network can modify or stop reporting by reconfiguring or removing the relevant measId, report configuration, or measurement object.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration) and clause 6.3.2 (MeasConfig), especially the MeasId, MeasObjectNR and ReportConfigNR definitions. MeasId associates a measurement object with a report configuration; ReportConfigNR defines event-triggered or periodic reporting behavior and reporting content/limits.

results.question: How does the UE handle a received condReconfigId when an entry with the matching condReconfigId already exists in the VarConditionalReconfig and the received entry includes a condExecutionCond?
results.reference: The UE replaces the existing condExecutionCond within the VarConditionalReconfig with the value received for this condReconfigId.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.13.3, Conditional reconfiguration addition/modification
results.model_answer: The UE replaces (overwrites) the existing VarConditionalReconfig entry identified by that condReconfigId with the received conditional-reconfiguration entry. Since condExecutionCond is present, the stored execution condition is updated to the received condition, together with the associated conditional RRC reconfiguration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (UE reception/processing of RRCReconfiguration), conditionalReconfiguration / condReconfigToAddModList processing: for a received CondReconfigToAddMod whose condReconfigId matches an entry in VarConditionalReconfig, presence of condExecutionCond causes the UE to replace the stored conditional-reconfiguration entry.

results.question: What action does the UE take upon receiving a condReconfigId in the condReconfigToAddModList IE when no matching entry exists in the VarConditionalReconfig?
results.reference: The UE adds a new entry for this condReconfigId within the VarConditionalReconfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.13.3, Conditional reconfiguration addition/modification
results.model_answer: The UE adds a new entry to VarConditionalReconfig for that condReconfigId, containing the associated conditional-execution information and conditional RRC reconfiguration. It does not treat it as a modification because no existing entry has the same ID.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (Reception of an RRCReconfiguration), processing of condReconfigToAddModList: for each condReconfigToAddMod, if its condReconfigId matches an entry in VarConditionalReconfig the UE replaces that entry; otherwise, the UE adds an entry to VarConditionalReconfig.

results.question: How is the condRRCReconfig value updated when the UE receives a condReconfigId that matches an existing entry and the received entry includes condRRCReconfig?
