results.reference: The UE sets absoluteFrequencyPointA to indicate the absolute frequency of the reference resource block associated with the random-access resources actually used during the random-access procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.10.5, RA information determination for RA report and RLF report
results.model_answer: The UE sets ra-InformationCommon.absoluteFrequencyPointA to the absoluteFrequencyPointA configured for the serving cell on which the reported random-access procedure was performed (i.e. the applicable ServingCellConfigCommon.frequencyInfoDL.absoluteFrequencyPointA). It is the DL carrier Point-A ARFCN from RRC configuration; it is not derived from the PRACH configuration index, msg1-FrequencyStart, or a measured SSB frequency.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3.3 (UE actions for UEInformationResponse/RA report construction), together with the RA-InformationCommon IE definition and field semantics in clause 6.3.2. The instruction for the field is to report the absoluteFrequencyPointA associated with the cell/carrier for the random-access information being reported.

results.question: What information does the UE include in ra-InformationCommon when the random-access resource used is associated with a CSI-RS?
results.reference: The UE sets the csi-RS-Index to include the index of the associated CSI-RS and sets numberOfPreamblesSentOnCSI-RS to indicate the number of successive random-access attempts linked to that same CSI-RS.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.10.5, RA information determination for RA report and RLF report
results.model_answer: The UE includes the index of the CSI-RS resource associated with the random-access resource used (i.e., the CSI-RS index) in ra-InformationCommon.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (RRC reconfiguration procedure, generation of RRCReconfigurationComplete/RA information). The procedure specifies that, when the RA resource used is associated with a CSI-RS, the UE reports the associated CSI-RS index in ra-InformationCommon.

results.question: How does a UE determine whether to apply the L2 U2N Relay UE configuration received in an RRCReconfiguration message?
results.reference: The UE applies the configuration if the rrc-Reconfiguration message includes the l2-U2N-RelayUE-Config and the UE is capable of supporting L2 U2N relay operation. If the UE is not capable, it ignores the field.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15, L2 U2N Relay UE configuration
results.model_answer: On reception of RRCReconfiguration, the UE processes sl-L2U2N-RelayUE-Config-r17 only when that IE is present and the UE supports/has indicated the L2 U2N Relay UE capability. In that case it applies the contained Relay-UE configuration as part of RRCReconfiguration processing. There is no PC5 discovery, relay-selection, or remote-UE request used to decide whether the dedicated configuration applies; those are operational procedures after configuration. If the IE is absent, no new Relay-UE configuration is applied. A UE that does not support the relevant Rel-17 L2 U2N relay feature cannot meaningfully apply the configuration.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, "RRCReconfiguration", UE actions on reception (including processing of the Rel-17 sl-L2U2N-RelayUE-Config-r17 IE). The associated ASN.1 definition and semantics are in clause 6.3.2, RRCReconfiguration non-critical-extension IEs / SL-L2U2N-RelayUE-Config-r17. UE support is established through the UE sidelink capability information defined in clause 6.3.6.

results.question: Under what conditions does a UE out of coverage on the concerned frequency for NR sidelink discovery, which is performing NR sidelink non-relay discovery, configure its lower layers for resource allocation?
results.reference: The UE configures lower layers to perform sidelink resource allocation mode 2 based on sensing using the pools of resources indicated in sl-DiscTxPoolSelected or sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal for NR sidelink discovery transmission on the concerned frequency in SidelinkPreconfigNR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.3, Sidelink discovery transmission
results.model_answer: The UE configures lower layers for autonomous resource allocation when it is out of coverage on the concerned NR sidelink frequency, is performing NR sidelink non-relay discovery, and has applicable sidelink discovery resource-allocation information in its NR sidelink preconfiguration (i.e., a configured/selected discovery transmit resource pool). The allocation is therefore based on preconfigured sidelink-discovery resources rather than a network-scheduled grant.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8 (Sidelink procedures), in the NR sidelink discovery/non-relay discovery procedure. The relevant conditional requirement is substantively: if the UE is out of coverage on the concerned frequency and performs NR sidelink non-relay discovery, it configures lower layers for resource allocation using the applicable sidelink preconfiguration/discovery resource-pool configuration. Exact subclause numbering can vary by 38.331 release.

results.question: How does a UE, which is selecting or has selected an NR sidelink U2N Relay UE and meets the Remote UE threshold conditions based on sl-RemoteUE-ConfigCommon in SidelinkPreconfigNR, proceed when it is out of coverage on the concerned frequency for NR sidelink discovery?
results.reference: The UE configures lower layers to perform sidelink resource allocation mode 2 based on sensing using the pools of resources indicated in sl-DiscTxPoolSelected or sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal for NR sidelink discovery transmission on the concerned frequency in SidelinkPreconfigNR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.3, Sidelink discovery transmission
results.model_answer: The UE shall perform (or continue) NR sidelink U2N Relay UE discovery on the concerned sidelink frequency using the preconfigured sidelink information. Being out of coverage does not prevent discovery; rather, when the sl-RemoteUE-ConfigCommon threshold conditions are met, it is a condition for the Remote UE to use the preconfigured NR sidelink discovery/relay-selection operation and to select or reselect a suitable U2N Relay UE according to the applicable relay-selection criteria.
results.evidence: Most likely normative evidence: 3GPP TS 38.304, clause titled "NR sidelink U2N Relay UE discovery and selection" (the Remote-UE behaviour for out-of-coverage operation and threshold-triggered relay discovery/selection). The associated RRC configuration source is 3GPP TS 38.331, the SidelinkPreconfigNR IE and its sl-RemoteUE-ConfigCommon field in the sidelink-related IEs clause.

results.question: What must be true for a UE capable of sidelink discovery to be configured by upper layers to transmit an NR sidelink discovery message?
results.reference: The frequency used for NR sidelink discovery must be included in either sl-FreqInfoToAddModList in sl-ConfigDedicatedNR within RRCReconfiguration and sl-DiscConfig is included in RRCReconfiguration, or the frequency must be included in sl-FreqInfoList within SIB12 and sl-DiscConfigCommon is included in SIB12.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.3, Sidelink discovery transmission
results.model_answer: In addition to supporting NR sidelink discovery, the UE must have an NR sidelink discovery transmission resource pool configured by RRC on the relevant sidelink frequency (i.e., a configured SL discovery Tx pool). Upper layers must not configure transmission of an NR sidelink discovery message unless such a discovery Tx resource pool is available/configured for the UE.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8 (Sidelink; NR sidelink discovery procedures/configuration) and the SL-DiscoveryConfigCommon-r17/SL-FreqConfigCommon-r16 definitions. The discovery configuration provides the sidelink discovery Tx resource-pool configuration (e.g. sl-DiscTxPoolSelectedNormal-r17, and where applicable exceptional-pool configuration); these resources are the prerequisite for upper-layer configuration of NR sidelink discovery-message transmission.

results.question: Under what conditions must an L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE include sl-Requested-SI-List in the RemoteUEInformationSidelink message, and why?
results.reference: The UE must include sl-Requested-SI-List when it has not stored a valid version of one or several required SIB(s) in accordance with clause 5.2.2.1. This is to indicate the requested SIB(s) to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.8.2, Actions related to transmission of RemoteUEInformationSidelink message
results.model_answer: An L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE includes sl-Requested-SI-List when it needs one or more on-demand System Information blocks of the serving cell of its selected L2 U2N Relay UE and does not already have a valid acquired copy of those SI messages. The list identifies the required SIB type(s) (and, where applicable, the UE's SI-version/value-tag knowledge). This is not an unconditional field: it is included only when SI acquisition through the relay is needed. The purpose is to let the relay/network know which SI the Remote UE requires, so that the relevant SI can be obtained/provided via the U2N-relay path rather than requiring the Remote UE to acquire it directly from the NR cell.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.7 (Sidelink relay procedures), in the L2 U2N Remote UE procedure governing transmission of RemoteUEInformationSidelink. The normative behaviour is expressed as a shall-condition for an L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE to include sl-Requested-SI-List when it needs SI of the selected relay's serving cell and does not have valid SI. Supporting ASN.1 evidence is the RemoteUEInformationSidelink definition containing the optional sl-Requested-SI-List, whose entries use SIB-TypeInfo.

results.question: How does an L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_INACTIVE determine the value to set for the UE specific DRX cycle in sl-PagingCycle-RemoteUE, and what identifiers must it include in sl-PagingIdentity-RemoteUE?
results.reference: It sets the UE specific DRX cycle to the minimum value of UE specific Uu DRX cycles configured by upper layer and configured by RAN. It must include both ng-5G-S-TMSI and fullI-RNTI in sl-PagingIdentity-RemoteUE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.8.2, Actions related to transmission of RemoteUEInformationSidelink message
results.model_answer: The L2 U2N Remote UE obtains its UE-specific paging/DRX cycle from the stored suspendConfig received in RRCRelease when it entered RRC_INACTIVE. It copies the UE-specific ran-PagingCycle value into sl-PagingCycle-RemoteUE (i.e., it does not independently select a sidelink paging cycle). In sl-PagingIdentity-RemoteUE it provides the identities usable for paging the inactive UE: its ng-5G-S-TMSI for CN-initiated paging and its fullI-RNTI for RAN-initiated paging. The shortI-RNTI is a resume identity and is not the paging identity for this purpose.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.1.3 (UE reception/processing of RRCRelease and transition to RRC_INACTIVE), especially storage/use of SuspendConfig including ran-PagingCycle, read with the ASN.1 definitions of RRCRelease/SuspendConfig and the sidelink remote-UE paging IEs sl-PagingCycle-RemoteUE and sl-PagingIdentity-RemoteUE. The paging identity types align with PagingUE-Identity: ng-5G-S-TMSI and fullI-RNTI.

results.question: What actions must an L2 U2N Remote UE take regarding the RemoteUEInformationSidelink message when entering RRC_CONNECTED, if it had previously sent sl-Requested-SI-List and sl-PagingInfo-RemoteUE?
results.reference: It must set both sl-Requested-SI-List and sl-PagingInfo-RemoteUE to the value 'release' and submit the RemoteUEInformationSidelink message to lower layers for transmission.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.8.2, Actions related to transmission of RemoteUEInformationSidelink message
results.model_answer: Upon entering RRC_CONNECTED, an L2 U2N Remote UE shall initiate transmission of a RemoteUEInformationSidelink message to the serving network when it had previously sent sl-Requested-SI-List and/or sl-PagingInfo-RemoteUE. The report carries the pending previously reported SI-request and/or Remote-UE paging information, so that the network receives that information directly after the Remote UE obtains an RRC connection.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3 (RRC_CONNECTED entry/actions). The normative condition is that an L2 U2N Remote UE which previously transmitted RemoteUEInformationSidelink containing sl-Requested-SI-List and/or sl-PagingInfo-RemoteUE initiates a RemoteUEInformationSidelink transmission upon entering RRC_CONNECTED. The detailed RemoteUEInformationSidelink transmission procedure and IE definitions are in the sidelink/Remote-UE information reporting procedures and message definitions of TS 38.331.

results.question: How does a UE determine which resource pool to use for monitoring NR sidelink discovery messages when it receives an RRCReconfiguration message with reconfigurationWithSync that includes sl-DiscRxPool?
results.reference: The UE configures lower layers to monitor sidelink control information and corresponding data using the resource pool indicated by sl-DiscRxPool for NR sidelink discovery reception in RRCReconfiguration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.2, Sidelink discovery monitoring
results.model_answer: The UE uses the NR sidelink discovery receive resource pool explicitly indicated/configured by sl-DiscRxPool. It applies that pool's resource configuration (i.e., the associated sidelink time/frequency resources and relevant PSCCH/PSSCH parameters) when monitoring NR sidelink discovery messages. The UE does not autonomously select another pool based on the synchronization reconfiguration; reconfigurationWithSync is the condition under which the sl-DiscRxPool instruction is applied.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE), in the UE processing for an RRCReconfiguration containing reconfigurationWithSync and sl-DiscRxPool: the UE is instructed to monitor sidelink discovery messages using the resource pool indicated by sl-DiscRxPool.

results.question: Under what conditions does a UE use the resource pool indicated by sl-RxPool in SIB12 for monitoring NR sidelink discovery messages?
results.reference: When the cell chosen for NR sidelink discovery reception provides SIB12, and sl-DiscRxPool is not included in SIB12, but sl-RxPool for NR sidelink is included in SIB12.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.2, Sidelink discovery monitoring
results.model_answer: A UE uses the SIB12 sl-RxPool for NR sidelink discovery reception when it is interested in NR sidelink discovery and SIB12 provides sl-DiscoveryConfigCommon (which contains sl-RxPool) for the serving cell. This is the common/broadcast discovery reception pool; it is not used merely because SIB12 is received if the UE is not interested in discovery. The applicable procedure is for a UE operating with the common sidelink configuration (notably RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3 (NR sidelink discovery procedures/configuration), together with SIB12 and SL-DiscoveryConfigCommon ASN.1 definitions in clause 6.3.1. The normative condition is expressed in substance as: if the UE is interested in NR sidelink discovery and sl-DiscoveryConfigCommon is present in SIB12, the UE uses the resource pool indicated by sl-RxPool to monitor NR sidelink discovery messages.

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding timers when it receives an RRCReject message?
results.reference: The UE must stop timers T300, T319, T319a, and T302 if they are running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.2, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: On reception of RRCReject, the UE shall stop T300. If the RRCReject contains the waitTime IE, the UE shall start T302 using the received waitTime value. No T302 start is mandated when waitTime is absent.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.5 (Reception of an RRCReject): the UE stops T300 and, when waitTime is included in RRCReject, starts T302 with the received waitTime value.

results.question: How does the UE handle the waitTime if it is configured in the received RRCReject message?
results.reference: The UE starts timer T302 with the timer value set to the configured waitTime.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.2, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: On receiving an RRCReject containing waitTime, the UE starts timer T302 with the received waitTime value (in seconds). While T302 is running, the UE shall not initiate a new RRC connection establishment procedure. When T302 expires, the establishment restriction is removed; if waitTime is absent, T302 is not started by that RRCReject.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3 (RRC connection establishment; UE handling of RRCReject) requires starting T302 when RRCReject includes waitTime. TS 38.331 clause 7.1.1 (timer T302) specifies that the UE shall not initiate the RRC connection establishment procedure while T302 is running.

results.question: What must the UE do if the RRCReject is received in response to an RRCResumeRequest or RRCResumeRequest1 and the resume was triggered for an RNA update?
results.reference: The UE must set the variable pendingRNA-Update to true.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.2, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall enter RRC_IDLE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.4 (RRC resume failure / handling of RRCReject): upon reception of RRCReject in response to RRCResumeRequest or RRCResumeRequest1, if the RRC resume was triggered for an RNA update, the UE shall enter RRC_IDLE.

results.question: How does the SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure support unicast communication by enabling the UE to report information about its associated peer UE?
results.reference: For unicast communication, the UE reports the sidelink UE capability information of the associated peer UE, the RLC mode information of the sidelink data radio bearer(s) received from that peer, and the sidelink DRX configuration and DRX assistance information received from the peer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR
results.model_answer: For NR sidelink unicast, a UE can send an UL-DCCH SidelinkUEInformationNR report containing the associated-peer-UE information IE (release/version dependent, e.g. sl-AssociatedPeerUE-Info). The report identifies the peer UE with which the reporting UE has a unicast/PC5 association and can carry the association-related information defined for that release. This gives the serving gNB visibility of the unicast peer relationship, allowing it to apply sidelink configuration and coordination—such as relevant resource, scheduling, or DRX-related decisions—to that UE's unicast sidelink operation. The procedure is a network report; it does not itself establish the PC5 unicast connection or carry unicast user-plane data.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3, "Sidelink UE information" (in particular the procedure initiation/reporting behavior), read with the ASN.1 definition of the SidelinkUEInformationNR message and its release-specific associated-peer-UE information extension. The clause specifies that the UE reports sidelink UE information to the network; the associated-peer-UE field provides the unicast peer-association information in releases where it is defined. Clause numbering and exact IE suffix may vary by TS 38.331 release.

results.question: In the context of groupcast or broadcast communication, what specific information related to DRX and service identification does the SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure allow the UE to report?
results.reference: For NR sidelink groupcast or broadcast communication, the UE reports the Destination Layer-2 ID and QoS profile associated with its interested services to which sidelink DRX is applied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR
results.model_answer: The UE can report its sidelink DRX preference/configuration information for groupcast or broadcast reception, together with the associated Service ID(s). The Service ID(s) identify the groupcast/broadcast service(s) to which the reported DRX information applies, allowing the network to configure or coordinate sidelink DRX on a per-service basis.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3 (SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure), together with the SidelinkUEInformationNR message/IE definitions in clause 6.2.2. The procedure text and associated sidelink-DRX information IE specify reporting of sidelink DRX preference/information for groupcast and broadcast communication and the corresponding Service ID(s).

results.question: What are the reporting actions related to DRX configuration rejection and relay operations that a UE can perform using the SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure?
results.reference: The UE reports DRX configuration reject information from its associated peer RX UE when acting as a TX UE with resource allocation mode 1, and reports parameters related to U2N relay operation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR
results.model_answer: Using SidelinkUEInformationNR, a UE can (1) report rejection of a configured sidelink DRX configuration—i.e., indicate that it cannot comply with the SL-DRX configuration received from the network—and (2) report relay-related interest/role information for Layer-2 UE-to-network relay operation, including that it is willing/interested to operate as an L2 U2N Relay UE or that it is a Remote UE seeking to use such a relay. These are UE-originated indications; they do not themselves activate or reconfigure DRX/relay operation.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (procedure titled "Sidelink UE information" / SidelinkUEInformationNR), together with the SidelinkUEInformationNR IE definitions in clause 6.2.2. The procedure specifies UE initiation to provide sidelink information to the network; the associated IEs include the sidelink-DRX rejection indication and L2 UE-to-network relay/Remote-UE indications (release-specific IE suffixes may differ).

results.question: How does the IAB Other Information procedure facilitate IP address management for the IAB-DU?
results.reference: It allows the IAB-MT to either request an IP address allocation from or provide an IP address to the IAB-donor-CU specifically for the collocated IAB-DU.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.12.1, General IAB-MT Network IABOtherInformation
results.model_answer: The IAB-donor-CU uses the IAB Other Information procedure to deliver IAB-DU IP-address information to the IAB-MT over RRC. The IAB-MT forwards that information internally to its co-located IAB-DU. This gives the DU a donor-provided/configured IP transport identity, rather than requiring the DU to obtain or infer it independently, and permits the address information to be updated when required. The DU can then use the address for its IP-based F1 transport connectivity toward the donor CU.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.2, "IAB other information". The procedure specifies that the IAB-donor-CU provides IAB-related information to the IAB-MT using the IAB-OtherInformation message; the IAB-MT delivers information intended for the IAB-DU to the DU, including IAB-DU IP-address information.

results.question: Why would an IAB-MT initiate the IAB Other Information procedure towards the IAB-donor-CU?
results.reference: To handle the IP address configuration for its collocated IAB-DU, either by obtaining an address from the donor or by reporting an already assigned address.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.12.1, General IAB-MT Network IABOtherInformation
results.model_answer: An IAB-MT initiates the IAB Other Information procedure to report IAB-node-specific information to its serving IAB-donor-CU, in particular the IAB-node address. The practical trigger is that this address becomes available or changes, so that the donor-CU can maintain the correct IAB-node identity/address association and use the current transport-relevant information for IAB control/DU connectivity.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7, subclause titled "IAB other information" (subclause numbering can vary by release): the procedure allows an IAB-MT to provide IAB-related information to the IAB-donor-CU through the IABOtherInformation message, including the IAB-node address.

results.question: What are the two specific actions an IAB-MT can perform using the IAB Other Information procedure?
results.reference: The IAB-MT can request the IAB-donor-CU to allocate an IP address, or it can inform the IAB-donor-CU of the IP address, both for the collocated IAB-DU.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.12.1, General IAB-MT Network IABOtherInformation
results.model_answer: An IAB-MT can use the IAB Other Information procedure to provide the IAB-donor-CU with (1) its IAB-node address and (2) its IAB-node name.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause titled "IAB Other Information" (IAB-MT-specific procedures). Its procedure description states that the IAB-MT may initiate the procedure to provide the IAB-node address and/or IAB-node name to the IAB-donor-CU.

results.question: Why does a UE need to reacquire MCCH information upon detecting an MCCH information change notification?
results.reference: The UE reacquires MCCH information because the notification indicates the MCCH information has changed, and the UE must acquire the updated configuration to receive the correct MBSFN services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2, MCCH information acquisition
results.model_answer: An MCCH information change notification is only an indication that the previously acquired MCCH is no longer current; it does not carry the replacement MCCH contents. The UE therefore reacquires MCCH so that it obtains the current MBS control information—e.g., current MBS session/service configuration and associated reception/scheduling/resource information—and does not continue receiving based on stale parameters. Reacquisition at the defined modification/acquisition timing also ensures that the UE applies a consistent version of the MCCH information.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.1.3, "MCCH information change notification" (within the MBS system-information procedures; exact subclause numbering can vary by release). The normative procedure requires a UE detecting the notification to acquire/reacquire MCCH according to the applicable MCCH configuration and modification timing.

results.question: What actions does the UE take regarding timer T310 when executing a reconfiguration with sync without any DAPS bearer configured?
results.reference: The UE stops timer T310 for the corresponding SpCell if it is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: For a reconfiguration with sync when no DAPS bearer is configured, the UE performs the normal (non-DAPS) handover behavior and stops timer T310 if it is running. Thus, any ongoing radio-link-failure detection associated with the pre-reconfiguration connection is cancelled; T310 is not allowed to continue through the normal reconfiguration-with-sync execution.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.4 (Reconfiguration with sync), in the non-DAPS-bearer branch: the UE shall "stop timer T310, if running" as part of executing the reconfiguration with sync.

results.question: How does the UE handle the C-RNTI and lower layers for the target SpCell when the reconfiguration with sync is for the MCG?
results.reference: The UE applies the value of the newUE-Identity as the C-RNTI in the target cell group, configures lower layers for the target SpCell in accordance with the received spCellConfigCommon, and configures lower layers in accordance with any additional fields included in the received reconfigurationWithSync.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: For an MCG reconfiguration-with-sync, the UE replaces its C-RNTI for the target SpCell with the C-RNTI (newUE-Identity) carried in reconfigurationWithSync. It then reconfigures the lower layers to apply the cell-group configuration contained in the masterCellGroup IE for that target cell group. Thus, the target SpCell is operated using the new C-RNTI and the target MCG lower-layer configuration, rather than retaining the source-SpCell C-RNTI/configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.4 (Actions related to RRCReconfiguration), in the processing of reconfigurationWithSync: for reconfiguration with sync for the MCG, the UE is instructed to consider the C-RNTI included in reconfigurationWithSync as the C-RNTI for the target SpCell and to reconfigure lower layers to apply the cell-group configuration specified in masterCellGroup.

results.question: What is the UE's action regarding SCells of the cell group that are not listed in the SCellToAddModList during a reconfiguration with sync for the MCG?
results.reference: The UE considers the SCell(s) of this cell group, if configured, that are not included in the SCellToAddModList in the RRCReconfiguration message, to be in deactivated state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: The UE shall release any configured SCell of the MCG that is not included in the SCellToAddModList when processing an MCG reconfiguration with sync.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (RRCReconfiguration procedure), in the handling of reconfigurationWithSync for the MCG: the UE is instructed to release SCells of the MCG that are not included in the SCellToAddModList.

results.question: What procedure does the UE perform if it is connected with a L2 U2N Relay UE when executing a reconfiguration with sync?
results.reference: The UE performs the PC5-RRC connection release as specified in 5.8.9.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: The UE performs the RRC re-establishment procedure. Specifically, when an RRCReconfiguration includes reconfigurationWithSync and the UE is connected with an L2 U2N Relay UE, TS 38.331 requires the UE to perform RRC re-establishment rather than execute the normal reconfiguration-with-sync mobility handling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.5 (Actions related to reception of RRCReconfiguration): for an RRCReconfiguration containing reconfigurationWithSync, if the UE is connected with an L2 U2N Relay UE, the UE shall perform the RRC re-establishment procedure. The RRC re-establishment procedure itself is specified in clause 5.3.7.

results.question: Under what specific RRC state and security conditions must the network ensure before initiating mobility from NR to a UE?
results.reference: The UE must be in RRC_CONNECTED with AS security activated, SRB2 and at least one DRB set up and not suspended.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The network shall initiate mobility from NR only when the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED and AS security has already been activated (i.e., security-mode control has been successfully completed).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (subclause titled "Mobility from NR", numbering may vary by release): "The network shall only initiate the procedure when the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED" and "shall ensure that AS security has been activated before initiating the mobility from NR procedure."

results.question: How might the network decide to trigger the mobility from NR procedure towards a UE?
results.reference: The network may initiate the procedure possibly in response to receiving a MeasurementReport or an MCGFailureInformation message from the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: TS 38.331 does not standardize the network’s mobility-decision algorithm. The network can configure NR/IRAT measurements (e.g., event- or periodical-reporting) and use the UE’s MeasurementReport, together with network-side information such as target-cell availability, load, policy and mobility robustness, to decide that mobility is needed. For a connected-mode handover, it then triggers the UE by sending RRCReconfiguration containing reconfigurationWithSync/mobilityControlInfo for the target cell; this may be NR-to-NR or NR-to-E-UTRA where applicable. If the intended action is release/redirect rather than handover, the network may instead use RRCRelease with redirection information. The actual threshold, ranking, and decision logic remain implementation/network-policy dependent.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5 (Measurements), especially clause 5.5.3 (Measurement reporting), together with clause 5.3.5 (RRC reconfiguration / mobility handling). These specify UE measurement configuration/reporting and the RRCReconfiguration mechanism used by the network to command mobility; they do not prescribe a mandatory network handover-decision algorithm.

results.question: What is the specific message sent by the network to command a UE in RRC_CONNECTED to perform mobility from NR?
results.reference: The network initiates the procedure by sending a MobilityFromNRCommand message to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: MobilityFromNRCommand. It is the DL-DCCH message used by the network to command a UE in RRC_CONNECTED to perform mobility from NR (e.g., toward a target RAT).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (Mobility from NR), together with the MobilityFromNRCommand message definition in clause 6.2.2: the network commands mobility from NR by sending MobilityFromNRCommand to a UE in RRC_CONNECTED.

results.question: What determines the UE requirements for the contents of SIB21?
results.reference: UE requirements are not defined by SIB21 itself, but are specified elsewhere, such as within procedures that use this system information or within the descriptions of the corresponding fields contained in SIB21.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.23, Actions upon reception of SIB21
results.model_answer: The UE requirement to acquire/use SIB21 is determined by the SI scheduling information in SIB1—principally whether SIB21 is listed in si-SchedulingInfo (via sib-MappingInfo), its si-BroadcastStatus, periodicity and scheduling window. SIB1 therefore determines whether SIB21 is broadcast or needs to be requested and when the UE is expected to acquire it. The network determines the actual SIB21 field values, subject to the SIB21 ASN.1/conditional-presence rules in TS 38.331; UE feature/release support determines whether the UE can apply feature-specific information carried by SIB21.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3 (Acquisition of an SI message), together with the SIB1 si-SchedulingInfo definition and the SystemInformationBlockType21 definition in clause 6.3.1. These specify that SIB1 schedules/maps SIB types to SI messages and indicates broadcast status; the SIB21 IE definition specifies its permitted contents. SI acquisition performance requirements are specified in TS 38.133.

results.question: How does a UE derive its operational requirements from SIB21?
results.reference: The UE does not derive requirements directly from SIB21. Any requirements are sourced from other specifications, such as the procedures that utilize the system information carried in SIB21 or the definitions of the information fields themselves.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.23, Actions upon reception of SIB21
results.model_answer: A UE does not infer generic operational requirements merely from the presence of SIB21. It first obtains SIB1, uses SIB1 SI scheduling information to identify the SI message carrying SIB21, receives that SystemInformation message in the applicable SI window (or requests it when configured as on-demand SI), and decodes the release-specific SIB21 IE. The UE then applies only those behaviours explicitly conditioned by the SIB21 fields, their presence/absence, and the UE's supported capabilities. Thus, SIB21 supplies broadcast configuration/parameters; the normative operational requirement is the corresponding 38.331 procedure's "UE shall" behaviour for each applicable field. Unsupported optional features are not enabled solely because SIB21 is broadcast, and absent fields invoke the ASN.1/procedure-defined default or mean that the associated feature/configuration is unavailable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2 (System information acquisition), read with clause 6.3.1 (the SIB21-rXX ASN.1 definition and per-field semantics for the applicable release). Clause 5.2.2 establishes that SIB1 provides SI scheduling/mapping and that the UE acquires the corresponding SI message; the SIB21 definition and its referenced procedures specify what the UE shall apply after decoding it.

results.question: Where must one look to find the UE requirements applicable to the information in SIB21?
results.reference: One must consult specifications outside of this clause, specifically the documentation for procedures that use the concerned system information and the technical descriptions of the corresponding fields contained within SIB21.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.23, Actions upon reception of SIB21
results.model_answer: Look in 3GPP TS 38.133 (NR; Requirements for support of radio resource management). TS 38.331 defines and signals SIB21, but it cross-refers the UE requirements applicable to its information to TS 38.133.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.2.2, IE SystemInformationBlockType21 (SIB21), whose descriptive text states that the UE requirements applicable to the information in SIB21 are specified in TS 38.133.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the RRC connection establishment procedure as described in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to establish an RRC connection, which involves SRB1 establishment, and to transfer the initial NAS dedicated information/message from the UE to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The primary purpose is to establish an RRC connection between the UE and the network, moving the UE from RRC_IDLE to RRC_CONNECTED and enabling dedicated signalling (including SRB1).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.1 (RRC connection establishment): "The purpose of this procedure is to establish an RRC connection."

results.question: When does an L2 U2N Relay UE in RRC_IDLE initiate an RRC connection establishment?
results.reference: It initiates establishment if any message is received from an L2 U2N Remote UE via SL-RLC0 as specified in 9.1.1.4 or SL-RLC1 as specified in 9.2.4.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.1, General
results.model_answer: An L2 U2N Relay UE in RRC_IDLE initiates RRC connection establishment upon receiving an RRCSetupRequest from a Remote UE (via the sidelink/PC5 relay path). The relay first establishes its own Uu RRC connection so that it can relay the Remote UE's RRC signalling towards the network.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.1 (RRC connection establishment — General). This clause specifies the normal upper-layer-triggered establishment case and includes the L2 U2N Relay UE-specific trigger: reception of an RRCSetupRequest from a Remote UE while the relay is in RRC_IDLE.

results.question: How does the UE determine the reference SS-RSRP value for the SpCell when the relaxed measurement criterion has not been met for T?
results.reference: The UE sets the reference SS-RSRP to the current SS-RSRP value of the SpCell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.13.1, Relaxed measurement criterion for low mobility
results.model_answer: When the relaxed-measurement criterion is not satisfied continuously for T, the UE shall no longer rely on relaxed-measurement operation and shall use the current SpCell reference SS-RSRP. The reference is derived from the UE's available SpCell SS-RSRP measurements using the configured SS-block measurement/averaging and L3 filtering rules (i.e., it is not a frozen value retained from the period in which relaxed measurements were applicable). The UE must then meet the applicable normal measurement requirements.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.1 (measurement requirements / application of relaxed measurements), read with TS 38.133 relaxed-measurement requirements and TS 38.215 SS-RSRP measurement definitions. The RRC specification delegates the detailed relaxed-measurement applicability and performance requirements to TS 38.133; the SpCell SS-RSRP used for the decision is the UE's measurement result derived under the configured SS-RSRP measurement and filtering rules.

results.question: Why would the UE set the reference SS-RSRP to the current SS-RSRP measurement of the SpCell?
results.reference: This occurs when the relaxed measurement criterion has not been met for the duration T, as specified in the procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.13.1, Relaxed measurement criterion for low mobility
results.model_answer: The UE sets this value to establish a serving-cell SS-RSRP baseline at the time the conditional reconfiguration is configured. That baseline is used by the conditional-reconfiguration evaluation procedure for the applicable reference/relative SS-RSRP condition, so that the decision is tied to the SpCell radio condition when the configuration was received rather than to an undefined or stale value. It provides a deterministic reference for deciding whether the configured condition has been met and, consequently, whether the stored conditional RRC reconfiguration may be executed.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, RRCReconfiguration procedure—conditional reconfiguration handling (the subclause numbering/title can vary slightly by release). The normative procedure states that, when handling the applicable conditional-reconfiguration configuration, the UE sets the reference SS-RSRP to the current SS-RSRP measurement of the SpCell.

results.question: What measurement quantity is used for both the current and reference L3 measurements in the relaxed criterion?
results.reference: Both measurements are based on SS-RSRP (SSB-based Reference Signal Received Power) for the SpCell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.13.1, Relaxed measurement criterion for low mobility
results.model_answer: SS-RSRP (i.e., SSB-based RSRP) is used for both the current and the reference L3 measurements when evaluating the relaxed criterion.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.12 (Relaxed measurement), in the relaxed-criterion evaluation text: the UE uses the SS-RSRP measurement quantity for both the current and reference L3 measurements.

results.question: How is the reference SS-RSRP value initialized according to the specified condition?
results.reference: When the criterion has not been met for time T, the reference is initialized to the current measured SS-RSRP value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.13.1, Relaxed measurement criterion for low mobility
results.model_answer: The question is under-specified: TS 38.331 does not define one global "reference SS-RSRP" initialization rule. Its initialization depends on the particular RRC procedure and the condition that triggers that procedure. Therefore, the reference value cannot be determined without the exact condition/clause (for example, a measurement-event, beam-management, SDT, or mobility condition).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence area: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5 (Measurements). The measurement procedures define SS-RSRP use, filtering, triggering quantities, and event-entry/leave handling per configured MeasObjectNR/ReportConfigNR; they do not establish a universal reference-SS-RSRP initialization applicable to all features. The applicable normative initialization text must be taken from the specific procedure containing the stated condition.

results.question: How does the UE update its measurement configuration when it receives new quantityConfig parameters for a specific RAT?
results.reference: The UE sets the corresponding parameters in its stored quantityConfig within VarMeasConfig to the values of the received parameters for that RAT.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.8, Quantity configuration
results.model_answer: Upon receiving a MeasConfig containing quantityConfig, the UE updates the configuration independently per RAT: for each RAT for which a quantityConfig is included, it replaces the currently stored quantityConfig for that RAT with the received one. A quantityConfig for a RAT that is not included is retained unchanged. The update is a replacement, not a merge of individual quantity parameters.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2, Measurement configuration: the UE processes quantityConfig on a per-RAT basis and replaces the current quantityConfig for each RAT included in the received quantityConfig. The QuantityConfig IE semantics further imply that RATs not included keep their current configuration.

results.question: Why might the UE stop and reset timers such as T321 or T322 during quantity configuration?
results.reference: The UE stops and resets these timers as part of reconfiguring measurement reporting for each measId in its list, ensuring outdated periodic or triggered reporting is cleared.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.8, Quantity configuration
results.model_answer: A new QuantityConfig can change the measured quantity and/or its Layer-3 filtering coefficients. Any running timer/state that was started using the previous quantity definition or filtered measurement history is therefore no longer valid. Stopping and resetting applicable timers (for example T321/T322 where the relevant procedure requires it) makes the UE restart evaluation with measurements filtered under the new configuration, preventing expiry or a subsequent action/report based on stale criteria. This is a configuration-change reset, not an indication that the timer condition has completed.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.4, "Quantity configuration", under MeasConfig processing. Read with clause 5.5.2 (measurement configuration) and clause 5.5.4 (measurement reporting): QuantityConfig changes measurement/filtering inputs, so measurement-related running state is re-initialized as specified by the applicable configuration branch.

results.question: How does the UE handle existing measurement reporting entries when applying a new quantity configuration?
results.reference: The UE removes the measurement reporting entry from VarMeasReportList for each measId included in its measIdList, effectively clearing previous reporting data.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.8, Quantity configuration
results.model_answer: When a new quantityConfig is applied, the UE removes all existing measurement reporting entries. Thus, reporting state/counters tied to prior entries are not retained; new entries are created again only as required by subsequent measurement-report triggering and reporting procedures.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration), quantityConfig handling: upon receipt of quantityConfig, the UE applies the new quantity configuration and removes all measurement reporting entries.

results.question: How does the network configure a UE in RRC_INACTIVE to provide SRS for positioning?
results.reference: The network provides the UE with a dedicated SRS configuration for positioning via the RRCRelease message, which includes the srs-PosResourceSet and srs-PosResourceSetId, allowing the UE to transmit SRS for positioning while remaining in RRC_INACTIVE state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.15, SRS for Positioning in RRC_INACTIVE
results.model_answer: The gNB configures positioning SRS for RRC_INACTIVE as part of the transition into RRC_INACTIVE: it sends an RRCRelease carrying SuspendConfig and, for the Rel-17 feature, the optional srs-PosRRC-InactiveConfig-r17 in RRCRelease-v1700-IEs. That IE configures the positioning-SRS resource sets/resources (including their applicable transmission characteristics). The UE retains this configuration in its inactive AS context and transmits the configured positioning SRS while remaining RRC_INACTIVE. A UE already in RRC_INACTIVE is not normally reconfigured by RRCReconfiguration; a changed configuration requires bringing it back to connected/resumed operation or providing a new release configuration during a subsequent release transition.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.8 (RRC release procedure), read with the RRCRelease ASN.1/message definition and the IE definition of RRCRelease-v1700-IEs containing srs-PosRRC-InactiveConfig-r17 (SRS-PosRRC-InactiveConfig-r17).

results.question: What is the specific criterion defined for Event I1 that leads to UE action?
results.reference: The criterion is the interference level becoming higher than a pre-defined threshold, which defines the triggering condition for Event I1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.10, Event I1 (Interference becomes higher than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event I1 is entered when the UE determines that the measured interference level becomes higher than the configured I1 threshold (after applying the configured hysteresis and time-to-trigger logic). Satisfaction of this entering condition triggers the event-based measurement-reporting action for the associated measurement identity/report configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.1 (event triggering criteria), Event I1: the entering condition is that the interference level is higher than threshold1; the UE applies the configured hysteresis and timeToTrigger before treating the event as triggered.

results.question: How is the triggering of Event I1 characterized in the specification?
results.reference: Event I1 is characterized by the interference measured by the UE becoming higher than a configured threshold.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.10, Event I1 (Interference becomes higher than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event I1 is characterized as an interference-threshold crossing event: it is triggered when the measured interference becomes higher than the configured threshold. The UE applies the configured hysteresis and timeToTrigger to the entering condition; reporting is initiated after the condition has remained satisfied for the configured timeToTrigger. It is therefore an absolute interference condition, not a serving-versus-neighbour cell comparison event.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.9, "Event I1": "Interference becomes higher than threshold" (clause numbering may vary slightly by release/version). The measurement-reporting triggering rules in clause 5.5.4.2 provide the general event evaluation behavior, including hysteresis and timeToTrigger.

results.question: What actions must a UE perform when it receives an sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList containing an sl-ReportConfigId that is part of its current configuration in VarMeasConfigSL?
results.reference: The UE must remove the matching sl-ReportConfigId entry from sl-ReportConfigList, remove all associated sl-MeasIds from sl-MeasIdList, and for each removed sl-MeasId, remove its reporting entry from VarMeasReportListSL and stop/reset its periodical reporting timer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.6, Sidelink reporting configuration removal
results.model_answer: For each listed sl-ReportConfigId that exists in VarMeasConfigSL, the UE shall remove the corresponding SL report configuration, remove every sl-MeasId associated with that sl-ReportConfigId from VarMeasConfigSL, and remove the related measurement-report entries (for those sl-MeasIds) from VarMeasReportListSL.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Sidelink measurement configuration / processing of MeasConfigSL), procedure text for sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList. The specified processing follows the pattern: remove the reportConfigSL, remove all associated sl-MeasId(s), and remove report-list entries associated with those IDs.

results.question: How does the UE handle the removal of an sl-MeasId that is associated with a removed sl-ReportConfigId?
results.reference: For each sl-MeasId removed from sl-MeasIdList, the UE removes its measurement reporting entry from VarMeasReportListSL if present, stops the periodical reporting timer, and resets associated information like sl-TimeToTrigger.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.6, Sidelink reporting configuration removal
results.model_answer: When an sl-ReportConfigId is removed, the UE shall also remove every sl-MeasId associated with that sl-ReportConfigId. This is an implicit/cascading removal; the corresponding sl-MeasId need not also be explicitly included in sl-MeasIdToRemoveList. Consequently, the UE no longer maintains or performs reporting for those sidelink measurement identities.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.3, "Sidelink measurement configuration" (subclause numbering may vary by release). In the processing of sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList, the UE removes the sl-ReportConfig having the indicated sl-ReportConfigId and removes all sl-MeasId associated with that sl-ReportConfigId.

results.question: What is the UE's expected behavior if the sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList includes an sl-ReportConfigId value not currently configured?
results.reference: The UE does not consider the message as erroneous; it simply ignores such non-configured IDs, as the note specifies no error handling is required for them.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.6, Sidelink reporting configuration removal
results.model_answer: The UE ignores that sl-ReportConfigId removal entry. It does not treat the received SL measurement configuration as erroneous, does not release any other report configuration, and continues using the remaining valid configuration.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.1 (Measurement configuration / processing of SL-MeasConfig; clause numbering may vary by release). The SL measurement-configuration processing specifies that an sl-ReportConfigId in sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList which is not configured is ignored.

results.question: Describe the sequential cleanup process triggered by removing an sl-ReportConfigId from VarMeasConfigSL.
results.reference: First, remove the sl-ReportConfigId entry from sl-ReportConfigList. Second, remove all associated sl-MeasIds from sl-MeasIdList. Third, for each removed sl-MeasId, clean up its reporting entry and timer/resources.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.6, Sidelink reporting configuration removal
results.model_answer: For each `sl-ReportConfigId` in `sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList`, the UE performs cascading state cleanup: (1) it removes the corresponding report-configuration entry from `VarMeasConfigSL.reportConfigList`; (2) it removes every `sl-MeasId` in `VarMeasConfigSL.measIdList` that references that `sl-ReportConfigId`; and (3) it removes the sidelink measurement-report state in `VarMeasReportListSL` associated with each removed `sl-MeasId`. This prevents further triggering, periodic reporting, or report accounting for a measurement identity whose report configuration no longer exists. The associated sidelink measurement object is not implicitly removed merely because its report configuration is removed; it is removed only by the applicable measurement-object removal processing.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.1 (Measurement configuration), sidelink measurement-configuration processing for `sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList` / removal of an `sl-ReportConfigId` from `VarMeasConfigSL`. The normative procedure specifies removal of the report configuration, removal of referencing sidelink measurement identities, and removal of their associated sidelink measurement-report-list entries.

results.question: Why would a UE initiate the procedure to report SCG failure information?
results.reference: The UE initiates this procedure to inform E-UTRA about a failure related to the Secondary Cell Group, specifically when the SCG transmission for an RRCReconfiguration message containing secondaryCellGroup fails.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3, SCG failure information
results.model_answer: A UE initiates the SCG failure information procedure when it detects that the Secondary Cell Group (SCG) can no longer be reliably used. The purpose is to inform the Master Node (MN), via the surviving MCG/RRC connection where available, of the SCG failure cause and associated SCG measurements so that the MN can recover, reconfigure, change, or release the SCG. It is therefore an MR-DC/DC recovery report, rather than an RRC re-establishment procedure for an MCG failure.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3.1, "SCG failure information -- General" (clause numbering may vary slightly by release/version). It states that the SCG failure information procedure is used by the UE to report SCG failure to the MN; the following initiation subclause specifies initiation upon SCG-failure detection.

results.question: How does the UE proceed after detecting an SCG failure related to reconfiguration?
results.reference: Upon detecting such a failure, the UE initiates the procedure to transmit an SCGFailureInformation message to the E-UTRA, as per the specified clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3, SCG failure information
results.model_answer: The UE treats a reconfiguration-related SCG failure as an SCG failure with failure type scg-ReconfigFailure. It stops using/suspends the failed SCG as specified and initiates the SCG failure information procedure toward the master cell group (MCG), sending SCGFailureInformation (normally via MCG SRB1) with the SCG failure cause and applicable SCG measurements. This is not, by itself, an MCG RRC re-establishment trigger; the UE remains connected through the MCG unless an independent MCG failure occurs.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.2 (SCG failure information procedure — initiation): the UE initiates the SCG failure information procedure upon detecting an SCG failure. The SCGFailureInformation failureType definition includes scg-ReconfigFailure for an SCG failure associated with reconfiguration. Related reconfiguration failure handling is specified in clause 5.3.5 (RRCReconfiguration procedure).

results.question: What actions must the UE take regarding timers T319, T319a, and T380 upon receiving an RRCResume message?
results.reference: The UE must stop timer T319 if it is running, stop timer T319a if it is running, and stop timer T380 if it is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.4, Reception of the RRCResume by the UE
results.model_answer: Upon receiving an RRCResume message, the UE shall stop T319, T319a, and T380 (if running).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13.4, "Actions related to reception of an RRCResume message"; the UE is instructed to stop timer T319, timer T319a, and timer T380.

results.question: How does the UE determine the contents of the interFreq-needForNCSG field when providing measurement gap and NCSG requirement information for NR?
results.reference: If requestedTargetBandFilterNCSG-NR is configured, the UE includes an entry in interFreq-needForNCSG for each supported NR band included in that filter and sets the NCSG requirement information for that band. Otherwise, it includes an entry for each supported NR band in interFreq-needForNCSG and sets the corresponding NCSG requirement information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.4, Reception of the RRCResume by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE evaluates its currently applicable NR inter-frequency measurement requirements. It includes interFreq-needForNCSG only when at least one required NR inter-frequency measurement cannot be performed without a non-cell-specific gap (NCSG). The field is an OPTIONAL affirmative indication (effectively "true"); absence means that the UE does not require an NCSG for its NR inter-frequency measurements. The determination is about the UE's measurement/RF capability and active measurement needs, not a request to apply a particular gap pattern.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration), in the subclause specifying UE provision of measurement-gap and NCSG requirement information for NR (NeedForGapsInfoNR / interFreq-needForNCSG). The normative rule is expressed as presence of the OPTIONAL affirmative field when the UE needs an NCSG for inter-frequency NR measurements.

results.question: What actions does the UE take for each sl-MeasId associated with a modified sl-MeasObjectId before reconfiguring the object?
results.reference: For each associated sl-MeasId, the UE removes its reporting entry from VarMeasReportListSL if present, and stops its periodical reporting timer while resetting associated information like sl-TimeToTrigger.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.5, Sidelink measurement object addition/modification
results.model_answer: For every sl-MeasId that references an sl-MeasObjectId being modified, the UE clears the event-trigger state before applying the new object configuration: it removes the associated entries from the triggered-cell/list-of-triggered-results state and stops any running time-to-trigger (TTT) timer associated with that sl-MeasId. It then reconfigures the sl-MeasObject. This prevents trigger decisions made using the old object parameters from being retained.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (SL measurement configuration / processing of sl-MeasObjectToAddModList). The normative processing for an existing sl-MeasObjectId being modified requires, for each associated sl-MeasId, clearing its triggered-list state and stopping its associated TTT timer(s), if running, before reconfiguring the sl-MeasObject.

results.question: When processing sl-MeasObjectToAddModList, under what condition does the UE add a new entry to sl-MeasObjectList?
results.reference: The UE adds a new entry when the received sl-MeasObjectId does not already exist in the sl-MeasObjectList within VarMeasConfigSL.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.5, Sidelink measurement object addition/modification
results.model_answer: The UE adds a new entry to sl-MeasObjectList when the sl-MeasObjectId of an sl-MeasObjectToAddMod entry does not match any existing entry in sl-MeasObjectList.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, sidelink measurement configuration processing (sl-MeasObjectToAddModList): for each sl-MeasObjectToAddMod, if its sl-MeasObjectId does not match an entry in sl-MeasObjectList, the UE adds a new entry to sl-MeasObjectList; otherwise, it modifies the matching entry.

results.question: Why does the UE stop the periodical reporting timer for sl-MeasIds associated with a modified sl-MeasObjectId?
results.reference: To reset the reporting mechanism and clear associated timing information (e.g., sl-TimeToTrigger) as part of reconfiguring the measurement object.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.5, Sidelink measurement object addition/modification
results.model_answer: The UE stops the periodic-reporting timer because modification of an sl-MeasObject changes the measurement object on which every associated sl-MeasId operates. Any already-running periodic reporting was established using the pre-modification object configuration; retaining its timer could therefore produce reports based on stale measurement assumptions. Stopping the timer resets the periodic-reporting state so that reporting is subsequently (re-)triggered and timed according to the modified sl-MeasObject. This is a normative state-handling requirement; the stale-configuration avoidance is its operational rationale.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.2 (MeasConfig / sl-MeasConfig processing; clause numbering can vary slightly by release). In processing sl-MeasObjectToAddModList, when an sl-MeasObjectId already exists and is modified, the UE is required to stop the periodical reporting timer, if running, for each sl-MeasId associated with that sl-MeasObjectId.

results.question: How does the offset parameter influence the triggering of Event A3?
results.reference: The offset parameter defines the threshold difference that must be met or exceeded; the neighbour cell's filtered measurement must be greater than the SpCell's filtered measurement plus the offset for the entering condition to be satisfied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.4, Event A3 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell)
results.model_answer: Event A3 is triggered when a neighbour cell becomes better than the SpCell by the configured A3 offset (after applying cell/frequency offsets and hysteresis). The entry condition is: Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Ms + Ofs + Ocs + Off, where Off is a3-Offset. Therefore, increasing a3-Offset raises the required neighbour-versus-serving measurement advantage and makes A3 harder/later to trigger; decreasing it makes A3 easier/earlier to trigger. A negative offset can allow triggering even when the neighbour measurement is slightly below the serving measurement, subject to the other offsets and hysteresis.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.4 (event-triggered reporting), Event A3: "Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell." The specified entering condition compares the neighbour measurement plus neighbour offsets, minus hysteresis, against the SpCell measurement plus serving offsets and the event offset (Off/a3-Offset).

results.question: Why does the specification include both cell-specific offsets and a general offset in the Event A3 evaluation?
results.reference: Cell-specific offsets allow for individual bias towards or against particular neighbour cells, while the general offset sets a common threshold, together enabling flexible handover optimization based on cell relationships and network topology.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.4, Event A3 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell)
results.model_answer: They serve different control scopes. The cell-specific offsets (Ocn and Ocp) let the network bias an individual neighbour and/or the SpCell, e.g. for cell-range expansion, load steering, coverage shaping, or a known preferred/avoided cell. The general Event-A3 offset (Off, configured as a3-Offset) is a common threshold applied to every A3 comparison; it sets how much better a neighbour must be before A3 is triggered. They are therefore not redundant: the effective per-neighbour bias is the relative cell bias Ocn−Ocp (also combined with frequency offsets), while Off controls the overall A3 triggering aggressiveness for the measurement configuration.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.4, "Event A3 (neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell)". The entering condition is specified as: Mn + Ofn + Ocn − Hys > Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off. The leaving condition is: Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off. Thus Ocn/Ocp are cell-specific terms on the neighbour/SpCell sides respectively, whereas Off is the Event-A3 offset common to the event configuration.

results.question: What actions must a UE take if upper layers abort the RRC connection establishment procedure due to an aborted NAS procedure, before the UE enters RRC_CONNECTED?
results.reference: The UE must stop timer T300 if it is running, reset MAC, release the MAC configuration, and re-establish RLC for all established RBs.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.8, Abortion of RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: Before entering RRC_CONNECTED, if upper layers abort RRC connection establishment because the NAS procedure is aborted, the UE shall stop T300 (if running), perform cell selection in accordance with TS 38.304, and enter RRC_IDLE. It does not proceed with RRCSetup completion or enter RRC_CONNECTED.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.5 (RRC connection establishment failure). This clause covers upper-layer abortion of establishment before RRC_CONNECTED and specifies stopping T300, performing cell selection, and entering RRC_IDLE.

results.question: How does the UE handle its MAC and RLC layers when the RRC connection establishment is aborted by upper layers prior to RRC_CONNECTED?
results.reference: The UE resets the MAC, releases the MAC configuration, and re-establishes RLC for all established Radio Bearers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.8, Abortion of RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: If upper layers abort RRC connection establishment before the UE enters RRC_CONNECTED, the UE resets MAC and releases RLC. Thus, MAC state is reset and the RLC entities/configuration established or used for the attempted connection are released.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.1 (RRC connection establishment — General), in the handling of an upper-layer abort before entry into RRC_CONNECTED: the UE is instructed to "reset MAC" and "release RLC" (with the detailed MAC/RLC behavior specified by TS 38.321 and TS 38.322 respectively).

results.question: What is the role of timer T300 in the procedure for aborting RRC connection establishment, and how is it affected?
results.reference: Timer T300 is stopped if it is running when the procedure is aborted by upper layers due to an aborted NAS procedure before RRC_CONNECTED is entered.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.8, Abortion of RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: T300 is the UE-side supervision timer for RRC connection establishment. The UE starts T300 when it initiates transmission of RRCSetupRequest. If T300 expires before successful establishment, the UE declares RRC connection establishment failure, aborts the establishment procedure, stops T300, and performs the specified failure/idle-mode actions. T300 is stopped when the UE receives RRCSetup (and establishment can proceed); it is also stopped as part of establishment-failure handling. Its duration is obtained from the broadcast UE-TimersAndConstants configuration (SIB1). Retransmissions/lower-layer access attempts do not imply a new independent establishment timer; T300 supervises the overall setup attempt.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3 (RRC connection establishment): the RRCSetupRequest procedure starts timer T300; receipt of RRCSetup stops T300; expiry of T300 triggers RRC connection establishment failure handling. See in particular clauses 5.3.3.4 (RRCSetupRequest), 5.3.3.5 (RRCSetup), and 5.3.3.7 (RRC connection establishment failure). The T300 value is provided in UE-TimersAndConstants in SIB1 (SystemInformationBlockType1).

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the counter check procedure as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is for the network to request the UE to verify the amount of data sent and received on each DRB, specifically by checking if the most significant bits of the COUNT for each DRB match the network's indicated values.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.1, General CounterCheck CounterCheckResponse
results.model_answer: The counter check procedure is primarily used to verify that the UE and the network have aligned PDCP COUNT values for configured DRBs. The network requests the UE's COUNT-MSB information and compares it with its own values, enabling detection of PDCP security/count synchronization mismatches.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.20.1 (Counter check — General): the procedure is defined for checking that the UE and network have the same COUNT values for radio bearers (operationally, the exchanged information concerns DRB COUNT-MSB values).

results.question: How does the counter check procedure help the network from a security perspective?
results.reference: It enables the network to detect packet insertion by an intruder acting as a 'man in the middle' by verifying the integrity of the COUNT values for each DRB.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.1, General CounterCheck CounterCheckResponse
results.model_answer: The CounterCheck procedure lets the network verify that the UE and network have consistent PDCP COUNT state for configured DRBs. This is security-relevant because PDCP COUNT is an input to AS ciphering and integrity protection. Detecting a COUNT mismatch helps prevent continued use of an inconsistent security context, which could otherwise cause deciphering/integrity failures and, in the worst case, increase the risk of COUNT reuse with the same key. The procedure is therefore a synchronization/verification mechanism; it does not itself establish new keys or directly authenticate the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10, "Counter check" (clause numbering may vary by release): the network sends CounterCheck and the UE returns CounterCheckResponse containing DRB COUNT-MSB information. The procedure enables the network to verify UE PDCP COUNT values. The security significance follows from the PDCP security use of COUNT specified in TS 38.323 and the AS security architecture in TS 33.501.

results.question: What specific aspect of the COUNT value does the UE verify for each DRB during the counter check procedure?
results.reference: The UE verifies if the most significant bits of the COUNT for each DRB match the values provided by the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.1, General CounterCheck CounterCheckResponse
results.model_answer: For each DRB, the UE verifies the most-significant-bit portion of the PDCP COUNT value (COUNT MSB), not the complete COUNT value. It compares the received COUNT MSB for the DRB with its corresponding locally maintained PDCP COUNT MSB.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause "Counter check" (UE actions upon reception of CounterCheck): the UE processes each DRB in drb-CountMSB-InfoList and checks the received COUNT MSB against the COUNT MSB of the corresponding DRB.

results.question: What type of radio bearer is the subject of verification in the counter check procedure?
results.reference: The procedure verifies the data amount for each Data Radio Bearer (DRB).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.1, General CounterCheck CounterCheckResponse
results.model_answer: The counter check procedure verifies Data Radio Bearers (DRBs), i.e., their PDCP COUNT state. It does not target SRBs.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.6 (Counter check): the procedure is specified for verification of COUNT values for DRBs. The CounterCheck message carries a DRB-CountMSB-InfoList, and CounterCheckResponse reports the corresponding DRB count information.

results.question: Under what conditions does the UE initiate the RRC connection resume procedure according to the clause?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure when upper layers or AS request resume of a suspended RRC connection. Specific AS triggers include: responding to RAN paging, triggering RNA updates while in RRC_INACTIVE, for NR/V2X sidelink communication per 5.3.13.1a, or for initiating SDT per 5.3.13.1b.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE initiates RRC connection resume only from RRC_INACTIVE, using its stored suspended AS context. It does so when it needs to access the network, notably: (1) upper layers request RRC connection establishment (e.g., MO signalling or UL data); (2) it needs to perform an RNA update (e.g., RNA has changed or the configured periodic RNA-update condition applies); or (3) it is paged for MT access and must respond. If the suspended context is unavailable/invalid, the UE uses RRC connection establishment rather than resume.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13, especially 5.3.13.2 (RRC connection resume procedure—Initiation), read with clause 5.3.3 (Paging) for paging-triggered access and the RNA-update requirements in the RRC_INACTIVE mobility procedures.

results.question: What must the UE ensure before initiating the RRC connection resume procedure?
results.reference: The UE shall ensure having valid and up to date essential system information as specified in clause 5.2.2.2 before initiating this procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: Before initiating RRC connection resume, the UE shall ensure that it has a valid stored UE Inactive AS context. This context contains, among other information, the resume identity and security-related state needed to form and protect the RRCResumeRequest.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13.1 (RRC connection resume — General): the UE is required to ensure that it has a valid UE Inactive AS context before initiating the RRC connection resume procedure.

results.question: How does the UE handle access control when resumption is triggered by response to NG-RAN paging?
results.reference: The UE selects '0' as the Access Category and performs unified access control procedure using that category and one or more Access Identities provided by upper layers. If the access attempt is barred, the procedure ends.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: For an RRC connection resumption initiated in response to NG-RAN paging, the UE does not perform access control (including UAC barring evaluation) before resuming. The paging-response case is an explicit exception to the normal access-control check for UE-initiated RRC establishment/resumption. The UE proceeds with the normal RRC resume procedure; this exception does not remove other applicable resume validation or procedure handling.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.14.1 (Access control—General). It specifies that the UE performs access control before initiating RRC connection establishment or resumption, except when the RRC connection resumption is initiated in response to paging from NG-RAN. Related procedure text is in clause 5.3.3.1 (RRC connection resumption—General).

results.question: How does the UE determine it is in MR-DC?
results.reference: The UE considers itself to be in MR-DC if and only if it is in (NG)EN-DC, NE-DC, or NR-DC.
