This is important because PDCP COUNT is an input to AS ciphering and integrity protection: continuing with inconsistent COUNT values can cause protected PDCP/RRC data to fail verification/decryption and undermines replay-protection/state consistency.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.9.1 (Counter check — General), together with the CounterCheck/CounterCheckResponse message definitions in clause 6.2.2. Clause 5.3.9 defines the procedure as the network requesting UE COUNT values for DRBs; it does not prescribe a mandatory network recovery action upon detecting a mismatch. RRC release/re-establishment or security reactivation is therefore a network implementation recovery decision, rather than an explicit mandatory CounterCheckResponse consequence in TS 38.331.

results.question: How does the UE determine when to initiate a measurement report for Event A4?
results.reference: The UE initiates a measurement report for Event A4 when the measurement result of a neighbouring cell becomes better than a configured threshold. This evaluation uses the entering condition formula Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh, where the result must remain satisfied for at least Time To Trigger to trigger reporting.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.5, Event A4 (Neighbour becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: For a measId configured with event-triggered ReportConfigNR/Event A4, the UE evaluates each applicable neighbour cell using the configured A4 measurement quantity and offsets. It starts the event when the entering condition Mn + Ofn + Ocn − Hys > Thresh is continuously met for timeToTrigger. At expiry of timeToTrigger, the UE initiates the event-triggered measurement reporting procedure (first report); further reports follow reportInterval/reportAmount. If reportOnLeave is configured, a leaving report may be sent when Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh is met for timeToTrigger.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.2 (event-triggered reporting / event A4 triggering conditions), together with clause 5.5.4.1 (measurement reporting procedure). Event A4 is defined as a neighbour cell becoming better than an absolute threshold; its entering condition is Mn + Ofn + Ocn − Hys > Thresh, subject to timeToTrigger.

results.question: How do the offset values Ofn and Ocn influence the triggering of Event A4?
results.reference: The offsets Ofn (frequency-specific offset) and Ocn (cell-specific offset) are added to the measured result Mn of the neighbour cell. They effectively adjust the measured value upward before comparison with the threshold, making the triggering condition Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh easier or harder to meet based on their configured values.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.5, Event A4 (Neighbour becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: For Event A4, the neighbour-cell measurement is evaluated after adding the neighbour-frequency offset Ofn and neighbour-cell offset Ocn. The entering condition is Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh. Thus, positive Ofn/Ocn raise the effective neighbour measurement and make A4 trigger earlier/easier; negative values make triggering harder. The corresponding leaving condition is Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh, so positive offsets also tend to keep the event entered longer. The condition must remain true for the configured timeToTrigger before reporting.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.4 (event-triggered reporting / Event A4 triggering criteria; clause numbering may vary by release): Event A4 uses the criterion Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh for entering, with Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh for leaving. Ofn is the frequency-specific offset of the neighbour frequency and Ocn is the cell-specific offset of neighbour cell n.

results.question: How does the UE determine when to initiate a measurement report for Event A6?
results.reference: The UE initiates a measurement report when the neighbour cell's measurement quantity becomes offset better than the measurement quantity of a configured SCell, as defined by the entering condition Mn + Ocn - Hys > Ms + Ocs + Off.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.7, Event A6 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell)
results.model_answer: For a measId configured with Event A6, the UE evaluates each applicable neighbour cell against the configured SCell using the configured trigger quantity (e.g., SS-RSRP, SS-RSRQ, or SS-SINR), after the applicable measurement filtering and offsets. It enters Event A6 when, continuously for timeToTrigger: Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Ms + Ofs + Ocs + Off. Mn/Ms are the neighbour/SCell measurement results; Ofn/Ofs are frequency-specific offsets; Ocn/Ocs are cell-specific offsets; Hys is hysteresis; and Off is the Event-A6 configured relative threshold/offset (the a6-Threshold parameter). When this entering condition has remained true for timeToTrigger, the UE initiates event-triggered measurement reporting according to the associated reportConfigNR. A leaving report may also be sent if reportOnLeave is configured and the leaving condition is met for timeToTrigger: Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Ms + Ofs + Ocs + Off.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4 (Measurement reporting), Event A6 ('Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell') under event-triggered reporting. The Event A6 clause specifies the entering condition Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Ms + Ofs + Ocs + Off and the corresponding leaving condition with +Hys; the event-triggered reporting procedure specifies reporting upon fulfilment of the condition for the configured timeToTrigger.

results.question: Why is the offset parameter 'Off' included in the Event A6 entering condition alongside the cell-specific offsets?
results.reference: The offset 'Off' is added to the SCell's offset measurement (Ms + Ocs) to provide an additional configurable threshold that the neighbour must exceed, allowing network-controlled adjustment of the reporting sensitivity for this event.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.7, Event A6 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell)
results.model_answer: Off is the event-A6-specific relative margin (the configured a6-Offset), not a duplicate cell bias. The frequency-specific (Ofn/Ofp) and cell-specific (Ocn/Ocp) offsets normalize or bias the neighbour and reference/SCell measurements according to measurement-object and per-cell policy. Off is then applied on the reference side to require the neighbour’s already-offset-adjusted measurement to exceed that reference by an additional configurable amount. This lets the network control A6 triggering/addition aggressiveness independently of persistent frequency/cell priorities, and prevents a report when the neighbour is only marginally better.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.2 (Event triggered reporting), Event A6 — “Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell”. The entering condition is specified as Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off, with Off defined as the offset parameter of the event. Its presence on the right-hand/reference side therefore creates an explicit required relative advantage for the neighbour.

results.question: Why is the RRC layer involved in the sidelink discovery procedure for announcement and monitoring?
results.reference: The RRC layer is responsible for configuring the parameters and resource pools used for both transmitting (announcement) and receiving (monitoring) sidelink discovery messages, as it handles the relevant configurations provided by pre-configuration, system information, or dedicated signaling.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13, NR sidelink discovery
results.model_answer: RRC is involved because sidelink discovery is an AS-controlled radio procedure: before a UE can announce or monitor discovery information, it needs RRC-provided/common and dedicated configuration for the applicable sidelink discovery resources and parameters. RRC distributes broadcast configuration (where applicable), applies network/dedicated configuration, and controls configuration changes/releases so that announcement transmissions and monitoring receptions use the resources and rules authorized for the UE and cell. RRC does not itself carry out the physical discovery transmission/reception; MAC/PHY perform it using the RRC-configured sidelink discovery configuration, while upper layers provide/consume the discovery service information.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3 (Sidelink discovery), especially the sidelink-discovery configuration procedure/general subclause, together with the ASN.1 definitions for SL-DiscoveryConfig-r17 and its common/dedicated discovery configuration. These provisions specify RRC handling/application of sidelink discovery configuration for UEs announcing and/or monitoring sidelink discovery.

results.question: How does a UE acquire the configuration necessary to monitor for sidelink discovery messages from other UEs?
results.reference: The UE acquires the monitoring configuration through RRC, which obtains it either from pre-configuration, system information broadcast, or dedicated signaling, specifying the resource pools to monitor for discovery messages.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13, NR sidelink discovery
results.model_answer: A UE does not blindly search arbitrary sidelink resources for discovery. It obtains the sidelink/discovery receive configuration from RRC configuration: normally the serving cell broadcasts the common sidelink configuration in SIB12 (SL-ConfigCommonNR, including the applicable discovery/common resource configuration), and the gNB can supplement or override it with dedicated sidelink configuration in RRCReconfiguration (SL-ConfigDedicatedNR and relevant release-specific discovery IEs). If no suitable cell configuration is available, e.g. out of coverage, the UE uses sidelink preconfiguration provisioned to it. The acquired configuration identifies the sidelink carrier/frequency, BWP, numerology, synchronization and the configured discovery receive resource pool(s); the UE monitors only those configured resources for discovery messages from peer UEs.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8 (Sidelink), in the sidelink configuration/discovery behavior, read with the SIB12 definition in clause 6.3.2 and the RRCReconfiguration/SL-ConfigDedicatedNR definitions in clause 6.2.2. These specify acquisition of common sidelink configuration through SIB12, dedicated sidelink configuration through RRCReconfiguration, and use of SL preconfiguration where network configuration is unavailable.

results.question: What conditions must be met for a UE to trigger Event Y1 according to the specified clause?
results.reference: Event Y1 is triggered when the PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and a candidate L2 U2N relay UE becomes better than threshold2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.19, Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and candidate L2 U2N
results.model_answer: Event Y1 is triggered on entry when the configured Y1 measurement quantity for the applicable measured cell/object becomes better than the configured y1-Threshold after applying the applicable measurement offsets and hysteresis, and the entry condition remains satisfied for the configured timeToTrigger. In generic form, the entry test is Q + offsets - Hys > y1-Threshold. If reportOnLeave is configured, leaving is detected using the reverse hysteresis direction (Q + offsets + Hys < y1-Threshold). The UE must also have an active measId whose associated reportConfig is Event Y1 and a valid measurement result for the configured trigger quantity.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.1, "Measurement reporting" / event-triggered reporting criteria, specifically the Event Y1 entry and leaving conditions. The clause defines triggering through the configured threshold, applicable offsets, hysteresis, and timeToTrigger; the exact quantity and offsets are those configured by the associated measurement object and report configuration.

results.question: How does the specification define the relationship between PCell quality and the candidate relay UE for Event Y1?
results.reference: The event requires two concurrent conditions: the PCell signal quality falls below a configured threshold (threshold1) while the signal quality of a candidate Layer 2 UE-to-Network relay rises above a different configured threshold (threshold2).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.19, Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and candidate L2 U2N
results.model_answer: Event Y1 is triggered when both conditions are satisfied: the PCell quality becomes worse than threshold1, and a candidate relay UE quality becomes better than threshold2. Thus, Y1 expresses a conjunctive condition: poor direct PCell quality together with a sufficiently good relay candidate; it is not triggered by either condition alone.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.1 (Event triggering criteria), Event Y1: “The PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and a candidate relay UE becomes better than threshold2.” The configured hysteresis and time-to-trigger apply to the event evaluation as specified for measurement-event reporting.

results.question: What role does the candidate node play in the triggering of Event Y1?
results.reference: The candidate node is specifically a Layer 2 UE-to-Network (L2 U2N) relay UE, and its signal quality must exceed a configured threshold (threshold2) to fulfill one part of the event's dual condition.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.19, Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and candidate L2 U2N
results.model_answer: For Event Y1, the candidate node is the entity whose measured radio condition is evaluated. The UE triggers Y1 when a configured candidate node satisfies the Y1 entry criterion (i.e., its measurement reaches/exceeds the configured threshold, subject to hysteresis and time-to-trigger). Thus, the candidate node is not merely reported as context; its qualification is the condition that causes the event.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.1, "Event triggering criteria" — the Event Y1 definition specifies the entry condition in terms of the candidate node meeting the configured measurement threshold/condition. The associated ReportConfigNR event configuration defines the threshold quantity, hysteresis and timeToTrigger.

results.question: Explain the dual-threshold mechanism involved in Event Y1 triggering.
results.reference: Event Y1 uses two separate thresholds: threshold1 for the 'worse than' comparison of the serving PCell, and threshold2 for the 'better than' comparison of the candidate L2 U2N relay UE. The event triggers only when both individual comparisons are satisfied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.19, Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and candidate L2 U2N
results.model_answer: Event Y1 is a conjunctive (dual-threshold) event: it enters only when both configured inequalities are satisfied simultaneously—i.e., the serving/reference-side measurement is below its first threshold and the relevant candidate/other-side measurement is above its second threshold (with the applicable offsets and hysteresis). It is therefore not triggered merely by crossing either threshold. The combined condition must remain true for the configured timeToTrigger before reporting is initiated. Hysteresis is applied with the opposite sense for leaving the condition, preventing rapid enter/leave reporting near either threshold. Threshold-1 and threshold-2 may be independently configured, so the event creates a guarded transition region rather than requiring one common quality level.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.1 (Measurement reporting), in the event-triggered measurement-reporting trigger conditions/table for Event Y1; the associated IE definitions are in clause 6.3.2 (MeasConfig/ReportConfigNR/EventTriggerConfig). The normative condition is expressed as two threshold comparisons combined by AND, with hysteresis and timeToTrigger handled by the general event-triggered reporting rules.

results.question: What information does the UE include in the plmn-IdentityList field of the VarRLF-Report, and what is the source of this list?
results.reference: The UE sets the plmn-IdentityList to include the list of Equivalent PLMNs (EPLMNs) stored by the UE. This list includes the Registered PLMN (RPLMN).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.5, RLF report content determination
results.model_answer: The UE includes the complete PLMN-IdentityList broadcast for the last serving cell (i.e., the PLMN identities associated with the cell on which the connection failure/RLF occurred). The list is taken from the cellAccessRelatedInfo.plmn-IdentityList in the latest applicable SIB1 received for that serving cell; it is not merely the UE-selected PLMN.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.3 (RLF report handling/content, release-dependent numbering), together with the VarRLF-Report IE definition and the SIB1 CellAccessRelatedInfo definition. The normative intent is that plmn-IdentityList in VarRLF-Report is populated from the PLMN identity list received in SIB1 for the last serving cell.

results.question: How does the UE determine the content for the measResultLastServCell field in the VarRLF-Report, and what time period do the measurements cover?
results.reference: The UE sets measResultLastServCell to include the cell level RSRP, RSRQ, and available SINR of the source PCell (for handover failure) or PCell (for RLF). These measurements are based on the available SSB and CSI-RS measurements collected up to the moment the UE detected the failure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.5, RLF report content determination
results.model_answer: The UE populates measResultLastServCell with the latest available measurement result for the cell that was serving the UE immediately before the connection failure/RLF. The result uses the applicable configured measurement quantities (e.g. RSRP, RSRQ and SINR when available) and is the UE's stored/filtered serving-cell measurement result, rather than a new measurement triggered after failure. The reported measurements represent the measurement information available for the 200 ms period immediately preceding the RLF declaration (connection-failure detection).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.3, RLF report / actions related to RRC re-establishment, which specifies how the UE populates VarRLF-Report, including measResultLastServCell and the measurement interval associated with the failure report.

results.question: Upon T331 expiry or stop, what does the UE release according to the specified procedure?
results.reference: The UE releases the VarMeasIdleConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.3, T331 expiry or stop
results.model_answer: Upon expiry or stopping of T331, the UE releases the DAPS source cell group (source MCG) configuration/resources, including the associated source-cell radio resources. This is a source-side release action; it is not, by itself, a release of the entire RRC connection.
results.evidence: Most likely TS 38.331 clause: 5.3.5 (RRC reconfiguration procedure), in the DAPS handover/source release handling text. The procedure specifies that, on expiry or stop of T331, the UE releases the source cell group configuration.

results.question: How does the UE handle idle/inactive measurements after T331 has expired or stopped during inter-RAT cell reselection to E-UTRA?
results.reference: It is up to UE implementation whether to continue measurements according to SIB11 and SIB4 configurations or according to E-UTRA SIB5 and E-UTRA SIB24 configurations as specified in TS 36.331.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.3, T331 expiry or stop
results.model_answer: After T331 expires or is stopped, the UE stops applying the NR-provided idle/inactive-measurement request/configuration in the E-UTRA reselection case. Thus, it does not continue the special idle/inactive measurements requested by the NR cell (nor retain them for later reporting as an active request). This does not suppress measurements needed for normal cell selection/reselection: once camped on E-UTRA, the UE performs the ordinary E-UTRA idle-mode measurements/reselection measurements required by the E-UTRA specifications.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.4.3 (cell reselection to E-UTRA), specifically the conditional UE behaviour associated with T331 having expired or stopped and idle/inactive measurements. The associated idle/inactive-measurement procedure/configuration is described in the TS 38.331 measurement procedures; ordinary E-UTRA idle-mode measurement and reselection behaviour is governed by TS 36.304/TS 36.331.

results.question: What implementation choice does the UE have regarding measurement configurations after T331 expiry or stop during inter-RAT reselection to E-UTRA?
results.reference: The UE implementation can choose to continue idle/inactive measurements either according to SIB11 and SIB4 configurations or according to E-UTRA SIB5 and E-UTRA SIB24 configurations from TS 36.331.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.3, T331 expiry or stop
results.model_answer: After T331 expires or is stopped in the inter-RAT reselection-to-E-UTRA procedure, the UE is allowed to either retain or release the stored measurement configuration(s). Releasing them is implementation-dependent; the specification does not require a single mandatory retention/release behavior.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.4.4 (cell reselection to E-UTRA), in the T331 expiry/stop handling text: the UE may release the measurement configuration(s), with the behavior being implementation-dependent.

results.question: How does a UE determine that an MBS service should be considered part of its MBS services of interest?
results.reference: The UE must verify three concurrent conditions: it is receiving or interested in receiving the service via a broadcast MRB; the service session is ongoing or about to start; and at least one MBS FSAI in the USD for this service is included in SIB21 acquired from the PCell for a frequency belonging to the set of MBS frequencies of interest.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.4, MBS services of interest determination
results.model_answer: A UE treats an MBS service as an MBS service of interest when the service identity advertised/configured for reception matches an MBS service identity supplied to the AS by upper layers. The match is based on the MBS service ID (and the associated PLMN/service context); where upper layers specify an MBS session ID, the session must also match. If no session ID is specified for that interested service, the interest applies to the service irrespective of session. This is an upper-layer-driven determination; receiving MBS system information or scheduling information alone does not make a service a service of interest.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8 (MBS procedures), in the MBS-service-acquisition/MBS-interest handling text defining the UE's "MBS services of interest" and its use of upper-layer-provided MBS service identity and optional session identity. Related normative ASN.1 evidence is the MBS-InterestInfo/MBS-InterestList information used for MBS interest indication, which carries an MBS service ID and optionally an MBS session ID.

results.question: How can a UE ascertain whether an MBS service session is ongoing?
results.reference: The UE may determine this from the start and stop time indicated in the User Service Description (USD).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.4, MBS services of interest determination
results.model_answer: A UE ascertains that an MBS service session is ongoing in the current cell by acquiring the current SIB20 and checking the MBS session-information list in the MBS broadcast configuration. If an entry matches the UE's target MBS service identity (TMGI and, where applicable, Session ID), the corresponding MBS session is ongoing/announced in that cell. The UE should refresh SIB20 after an SI-change indication; absence of a matching entry means that the session is not currently announced as ongoing in that cell, not necessarily that it is unavailable elsewhere.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.1 (System information acquisition), together with the SIB20/MBS broadcast configuration ASN.1 definitions in clause 6.3 (in particular SystemInformationBlockType20-r17, MBS-BroadcastConfiguration-r17 and MBS-SessionInfo-r17). These specify SIB20 as the broadcast source of MBS session information and provide the TMGI/session identity used for session identification.

results.question: How does the UE set the contents of the UEAssistanceInformation message when initiating transmission to provide a delay budget report?
results.reference: The UE sets the delayBudgetReport field to type1 according to a desired value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.3, Actions related to transmission of UEAssistanceInformation message
results.model_answer: When the UE initiates UEAssistanceInformation to provide a delay budget report, it includes the delayBudgetReport IE and sets its contents from the delay-budget-report information indicated by upper layers. RRC does not derive or modify the reported delay budget; it conveys the upper-layer-provided report, including the applicable DRB/report entries, in UEAssistanceInformation.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.4.2 (UE assistance information procedure — Initiation): the UE, when providing a delay budget report, sets the delayBudgetReport field in UEAssistanceInformation in accordance with the information indicated by upper layers. Exact clause numbering/title can vary slightly by TS 38.331 release version.

results.question: How does the UE configure the OverheatingAssistance IE when it prefers to temporarily reduce the maximum aggregated bandwidth of FR1?
results.reference: The UE includes reducedMaxBW-FR1 in the OverheatingAssistance IE, sets reducedBW-DL to the preferred maximum aggregated bandwidth for downlink carriers of FR1, and sets reducedBW-UL to the preferred maximum aggregated bandwidth for uplink carriers of FR1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.3, Actions related to transmission of UEAssistanceInformation message
results.model_answer: The UE includes OverheatingAssistance in UEAssistanceInformation and sets reducedMaxBW-FR1-r16 to the enumerated value representing its preferred temporary FR1 maximum aggregated bandwidth: mhz20, mhz40, mhz60, mhz80, or mhz100. The indicated value is a temporary UE preference/assistance indication to the network; it is not itself an RRC bandwidth reconfiguration. It is independent of reducedMaxCCs-r16, which instead indicates a preferred reduction in the number of aggregated component carriers.
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.4 (Overheating assistance, UE assistance information procedure), together with the OverheatingAssistance-r16 ASN.1 definition in clause 6.3.2. The procedure text specifies use of reducedMaxBW-FR1-r16 when the UE prefers to temporarily reduce its maximum aggregated bandwidth in FR1.

results.question: What steps does the UE follow to indicate a preference for temporarily reducing the number of maximum MIMO layers for each serving cell operating on FR2-1 for the SCG?
results.reference: The UE includes reducedMaxMIMO-LayersFR2 in the OverheatingAssistance IE, sets reducedMIMO-LayersFR2-DL to the preferred number of maximum MIMO layers for downlink, and sets reducedMIMO-LayersFR2-UL to the preferred number for uplink.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.3, Actions related to transmission of UEAssistanceInformation message
results.model_answer: The UE initiates the UEAssistanceInformation procedure and sends UEAssistanceInformation containing the reducedMaxMIMO-LayerPreference applicable to the SCG. It includes one per-serving-cell preference entry for every SCG serving cell operating in FR2-1 for which it requests a temporary reduction. Each entry identifies the SCG serving cell and indicates the preferred reduced maximum number of DL and/or UL MIMO layers, as applicable. This is an assistance/preference indication only: the UE does not autonomously change the configured MIMO-layer capability or transmission configuration; the network/SN decides whether and how to apply the preference.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.4 (UE assistance information procedure), together with the UEAssistanceInformation message and the reducedMaxMIMO-LayerPreference IE definitions in clause 6.2.2/6.3. The Rel-17 version of the IE is applicable where the specification distinguishes FR2-1 and SCG handling.

results.question: How does the UE determine the filtering coefficient 'a' for a measurement quantity when performing layer 3 filtering for a MeasObjectNR?
results.reference: For MeasObjectNR, the UE calculates a = 1/2^(k_i/4), where k_i is the filterCoefficient for the corresponding measurement quantity of the i-th QuantityConfigNR in quantityConfigNR-List, and i is indicated by the quantityConfigIndex in the MeasObjectNR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.3.2, Layer 3 filtering
results.model_answer: The MeasObjectNR does not directly carry the L3 coefficient. The UE selects the applicable FilterConfigNR from the QuantityConfigNR associated with the MeasObjectNR (via quantityConfigIndex, using the SSB or CSI-RS filter configuration as applicable), then selects the coefficient field for the measured quantity: filterCoefficientRSRP, filterCoefficientRSRQ, or filterCoefficientRS-SINR. If the configured FilterCoefficient is fcK, the UE uses k=K and computes a=2^(-k/4). If that coefficient is not configured, it uses fc0, i.e. k=0 and a=1 (no temporal smoothing). The filtered value is recursively formed as F_n=(1-a)F_(n-1)+aM_n.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.3.2 (Layer 3 filtering), together with the QuantityConfigNR/FilterConfigNR ASN.1 definitions in clause 6.3.2. The clause specifies a=1/2^(k/4), where k is the configured FilterCoefficient value.

results.question: Under what condition is no layer 3 filtering applied to a measurement quantity, and how is this indicated in the configuration?
results.reference: No layer 3 filtering is applicable if the filterCoefficient k is set to 0. This is explicitly stated in Note 1 of the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.3.2, Layer 3 filtering
results.model_answer: No Layer-3 filtering is applied when the configured FilterCoefficient for the relevant measurement quantity is fc0. This is indicated by setting the applicable filterCoefficientRSRP, filterCoefficientRSRQ, or filterCoefficientSINR field in QuantityConfig to the ENUMERATED value fc0.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.3.2 (Measurement configuration / ASN.1 definitions): the FilterCoefficient enumeration defines fc0 as corresponding to no Layer-3 filtering.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the RRC connection release procedure as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to release the RRC connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.9.1, General
results.model_answer: Its primary purpose is to release the UE's RRC connection, i.e., transition the UE out of RRC_CONNECTED as directed by the network. The RRCRelease message can additionally support actions such as RRC connection suspension or redirection, but these are extensions of the release procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.8.1 (RRC connection release — General): the procedure is defined for releasing an RRC connection.

results.question: How might the RRC connection release procedure affect UE access to the current PCell?
results.reference: Access to the current PCell may be barred as a result of this procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.9.1, General
results.model_answer: RRCRelease can make return to the current PCell less likely, but it does not by itself bar the cell. In particular, if RRCRelease includes deprioritisationReq, the UE applies the requested deprioritisation to the current PCell's frequency or RAT for the indicated timer. Consequently, after entering RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE, the UE should prefer eligible higher-priority alternatives and may not reselect the former PCell while the deprioritisation applies. redirectedCarrierInfo or cellReselectionPriorities may similarly steer the UE away from that PCell. Without such information, the UE performs normal cell selection/reselection and may camp on the same cell again if it remains suitable and not barred.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.8.3 (Reception of RRCRelease by the UE): upon reception of RRCRelease, the UE processes redirectedCarrierInfo, cellReselectionPriorities, suspend configuration, and, when deprioritisationReq is present, applies deprioritisation to the frequency or RAT of the current PCell as indicated.

results.question: How does the UE determine when to initiate the procedure upon RRCReject reception?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure if the access attempt is barred during an attempt to establish or resume an RRC connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.1, Initiation
results.model_answer: On reception of RRCReject, the UE uses the reject's optional wait indication to control re-attempt timing. If waitTime is included, the UE starts T302 with that value; if extendedWaitTime is included, it starts T302 with the extended value. The UE then performs cell selection, and while T302 is running it treats the rejecting cell as barred under TS 38.304. Therefore, a new setup attempt on that cell is deferred until the T302-based barring ends; the UE may instead select an eligible alternative cell. If no wait indication is present, there is no T302 wait imposed by the RRCReject and normal cell-selection/setup-initiation rules apply.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.5, "Reception of an RRCReject by the UE" (most likely evidence clause): the UE starts T302 using waitTime or extendedWaitTime when present, performs cell selection according to TS 38.304, and considers the cell barred while T302 is running.

results.question: What triggers the UE to start the procedure upon receiving RRCReject?
results.reference: The trigger occurs when the UE's access attempt is barred while trying to establish or resume an RRC connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.1, Initiation
results.model_answer: Reception of an RRCReject invokes the RRCReject handling. The UE starts timer T302 only when the RRCReject contains the waitTime IE; the timer value is set to that waitTime value. Thus, the presence of waitTime is the specific trigger for starting T302 (and the associated establishment back-off).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.2.3 (Actions upon reception of RRCReject): "if the RRCReject message includes the waitTime: start timer T302, with the timer value set to the waitTime."

results.question: What two actions does the UE take regarding the periodical reporting timer when submitting a MeasurementReportSidelink message for a triggered measurement?
results.reference: First, the UE stops the periodical reporting timer if it is running. Then, if the number of reports sent is less than the configured report amount, the UE starts the timer again with the value of the sl-ReportInterval from the corresponding report configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.5.1, General MeasurementReportSidelink
results.model_answer: The UE stops the periodical reporting timer if it is running, and then starts/restarts it with the configured reportInterval value.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.7 (measurement reporting), event-triggered sidelink measurement reporting procedure for MeasurementReportSidelink: the procedure specifies stopping the periodical reporting timer, if running, and starting it with reportInterval when the triggered report is submitted.

results.question: What is the initial step the UE performs for the sl-MeasId when setting the contents of the MeasurementReportSidelink message?
results.reference: The UE sets the sl-MeasId field within the message to the specific measurement identity that originally triggered the NR sidelink measurement reporting procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.5.1, General MeasurementReportSidelink
results.model_answer: The UE first sets the measId field of the MeasurementReportSidelink message to the applicable sl-MeasId.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, sidelink measurement-reporting procedure (the clause titled "Sidelink measurement reporting" / procedure for setting the contents of MeasurementReportSidelink). Its first listed action is: "set the measId field to sl-MeasId."

results.question: How are the boundaries of the eDRX acquisition period determined for UEs using an eDRX cycle longer than the modification period?
results.reference: The boundaries are determined by Hyper-SFN values where H-SFN modulo 1024 equals 0.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.2.2, SI change indication and PWS notification
results.model_answer: For an eDRX cycle longer than the modification period, the eDRX acquisition period is bounded by modification-period boundaries: it starts at the beginning of the modification period in which the UE monitors its Paging Occasion, and ends at the end of the immediately following modification period. Thus, it covers the paging/notification modification period and the next modification period in which updated SI can take effect.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2 (System information), in the SI-acquisition/eDRX-acquisition-period UE behaviour text. The relevant rule specifies the eDRX acquisition-period start and end for the case where the eDRX cycle is longer than the modification period.

results.question: Under what condition must a UE in RRC_INACTIVE monitor for SI change indication in any paging occasion at least once per modification period?
results.reference: When the timer T319a is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.2.2, SI change indication and PWS notification
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_INACTIVE must monitor for an SI change indication in any paging occasion at least once per modification period when it is configured with an extended DRX (eDRX) cycle that is longer than the SI modification period.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3 (SI change indication): the RRC_INACTIVE UE requirement to monitor an SI-change indication in any paging occasion at least once per modification period applies when its configured eDRX cycle exceeds the modification period.

results.question: What action must a UE configured with an RRC_IDLE eDRX cycle longer than the modification period take if the systemInfoModification-eDRX bit of the Short Message is set?
results.reference: It must apply the SI acquisition procedure defined in clause 5.2.2.3 from the start of the next eDRX acquisition period boundary.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.2.2, SI change indication and PWS notification
results.model_answer: The UE shall immediately re-acquire the required system information (i.e., initiate SI acquisition without waiting for the next modification-period boundary).
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.3.2, "System information change notification." The UE behavior for a received Short Message with systemInfoModification-eDRX set is to acquire SI immediately when its configured eDRX cycle is longer than the modification period.

results.question: How does the clause specify the handling of SIB6, SIB7, or SIB8 acquisition if they overlap with a measurement gap?
results.reference: It is left to UE implementation how to immediately acquire these SIBs in such an overlap scenario.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.2.2, SI change indication and PWS notification
results.model_answer: The UE gives acquisition of SIB6, SIB7, or SIB8 priority over measurement-gap use. If the relevant SI window overlaps a configured measurement gap, the UE acquires the warning SIB during that gap; it is not required to perform measurements in the overlapping gap.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2 (System information acquisition), in the SI-message acquisition requirements for SIB6/SIB7/SIB8. The requirement states in substance that, when the SI window for SIB6, SIB7 or SIB8 overlaps a measurement gap, the UE shall acquire the applicable SIB during the measurement gap and is not required to perform measurements in that gap.

results.question: How does the UE process an sl-MeasId that already exists in its VarMeasConfigSL when it receives an sl-MeasIdToAddModList?
results.reference: The UE replaces the existing entry in the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL with the new value received for that sl-MeasId.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.3, Sidelink measurement identity addition/modification
results.model_answer: For each entry in sl-MeasIdToAddModList, if its sl-MeasId already exists in VarMeasConfigSL, the UE replaces (modifies) the existing sl-MeasId configuration with the received entry. It does not create a duplicate; the updated entry includes the received associations, e.g. sl-MeasObjectId and sl-ReportConfigId.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.5.1 (sidelink measurement configuration / MeasConfigSL processing): the UE processing rule for sl-MeasIdToAddModList specifies that, when an sl-MeasId is already present in VarMeasConfigSL, the UE replaces the existing sl-MeasId with the received sl-MeasId.

results.question: What actions does the UE take regarding reporting when modifying an existing sl-MeasId from the sl-MeasIdToAddModList?
results.reference: The UE removes the measurement reporting entry for that sl-MeasId from the VarMeasReportListSL if present, stops the periodical reporting timer, and resets associated information like sl-TimeToTrigger.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.3, Sidelink measurement identity addition/modification
results.model_answer: When an sl-MeasId in sl-MeasIdToAddModList already exists, the UE stops the measurement reporting associated with that existing sl-MeasId before applying the modified association/configuration. Reporting is subsequently governed by the newly configured sl-MeasId; the UE must not continue reporting under the old association.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.1a (Sidelink measurement configuration), processing of sl-MeasIdToAddModList: modification of an already configured sl-MeasId requires the UE to stop the associated measurement reporting and update/reconfigure the sl-MeasId.

results.question: How does the UE handle a new sl-MeasId received in the sl-MeasIdToAddModList that does not match any existing entry?
results.reference: The UE adds a new entry for this sl-MeasId within the VarMeasConfigSL.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.3, Sidelink measurement identity addition/modification
results.model_answer: The UE adds a new sidelink measurement-identity entry to its stored sl-MeasIdList. The new entry is keyed by the received sl-MeasId and associates the received sl-MeasObjectId and sl-ReportConfigId. It is not treated as an error or ignored merely because no existing sl-MeasId entry matches.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.2 (Measurement configuration), processing of sl-MeasIdToAddModList. The specified add/modify logic is: if the received sl-MeasId matches an entry in the UE's sl-MeasIdList, modify that entry; otherwise, add a new entry to sl-MeasIdList.

results.question: What is the UE's procedure when it receives an sl-MeasIdToAddModList containing multiple sl-MeasIds?
results.reference: The UE processes each sl-MeasId included in the received list individually, performing the appropriate addition, modification, and reporting cleanup actions per the specified rules.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.3, Sidelink measurement identity addition/modification
results.model_answer: The UE processes every entry in sl-MeasIdToAddModList; it does not select only one sl-MeasId. For each listed sl-MeasId, it adds a new sidelink measurement identity or modifies the existing identity with that ID in its sidelink measurement-identity list. Each identity associates an sl-MeasObjectId with an sl-ReportConfigId, so multiple entries can establish/modify multiple independent sidelink measurement/reporting associations. If the same sl-MeasId is repeated, the effective configuration is the modification resulting from processing the applicable entry (i.e., the later entry when processed in list order).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.6.1 (Sidelink measurement configuration). The sl-MeasIdToAddModList handling states, in substance: when the list is present, for each sl-MeasId entry in the list, the UE adds or modifies the sl-MeasId entry in its sidelink measurement identity list.

results.question: How does a UE recover from a detected physical layer problem on its SpCell when T310 is running?
results.reference: The UE recovers by stopping timers T310 and T312 upon receiving N311 consecutive 'in-sync' indications from lower layers for the SpCell while T310 is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.2, Recovery of physical layer problems
results.model_answer: While T310 is running for the SpCell, the UE recovers if lower layers deliver N311 consecutive in-sync indications. The UE shall stop T310; therefore no radio link failure is declared. If the required in-sync indications are not received and T310 expires, the UE detects RLF for the SpCell and proceeds with the applicable RRC re-establishment/RLF handling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.1 (Detection of radio link failure): upon receiving N311 consecutive in-sync indications from lower layers while T310 is running, the UE shall stop T310. The same RLF detection procedure specifies that expiry of T310 started for the SpCell causes the UE to consider RLF detected in the SpCell.

results.question: What specific UE actions are triggered upon receiving N311 consecutive 'in-sync' indications for the SpCell while timer T310 is active?
results.reference: The UE shall stop timer T310 for that SpCell and also stop timer T312 for that SpCell if it is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.2, Recovery of physical layer problems
results.model_answer: The UE shall stop timer T310 upon receiving N311 consecutive in-sync indications from lower layers for the SpCell while T310 is running. No radio link failure is declared by this event; stopping T310 prevents its expiry-based RLF detection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.1 (Radio link failure detection): upon receiving N311 consecutive in-sync indications from lower layers while T310 is running, the UE shall stop timer T310.

results.question: How do periods without L1 reporting affect the counting of consecutive 'in-sync' or 'out-of-sync' indications for physical layer problem recovery?
results.reference: Periods where neither 'in-sync' nor 'out-of-sync' is reported by layer 1 do not affect the evaluation of the number of consecutive indications.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.2, Recovery of physical layer problems
results.model_answer: A period in which L1 provides no in-sync/out-of-sync indication is neutral: it neither increments a counter nor breaks/resets the current consecutive-indication count. Counting resumes with the next actual L1 indication. Thus, N310 is reached only after N310 actual consecutive out-of-sync indications, and, while T310 runs, N311 is reached only after N311 actual consecutive in-sync indications; an opposite indication breaks the respective run, but mere absence of reporting does not.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.1 (Detection of radio link failure). Its RLF procedure is driven by receipt of N310 consecutive out-of-sync indications and N311 consecutive in-sync indications from lower layers. It specifies actions on received indications (start T310 after N310 out-of-sync; stop T310 after N311 in-sync), not on elapsed intervals without indications. Therefore no-reporting intervals are not themselves indications and do not alter the consecutive-count state.

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE in RRC_CONNECTED acquire the MIB?
results.reference: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED must acquire the MIB only while the T311 timer is running. The clause specifies that for MIB acquisition, the UE shall act if it is in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, or in RRC_CONNECTED while T311 is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.1, Acquisition of MIB and SIB1
results.model_answer: In RRC_CONNECTED, the UE must acquire the MIB of the target SpCell when it receives an RRCReconfiguration containing reconfigurationWithSync. This covers synchronization to a new PCell in handover and synchronization to a new PSCell in dual-connectivity/PSCell-change procedures. It is not a general requirement to continuously reacquire the MIB merely because the UE remains RRC_CONNECTED or because other system information changes.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.5 (RRCReconfiguration), in the UE actions for reconfigurationWithSync: the UE performs synchronization to the target SpCell and acquires the MIB of the target cell. Clause 5.2.1 (MIB acquisition) provides the associated MIB-acquisition procedure.

results.question: What are the three specific scenarios that trigger a requirement for a UE in RRC_CONNECTED (with an active BWP configured with searchSpaceSIB1) to acquire SIB1?
results.reference: The three scenarios are: 1) The UE has received an indication about a change of system information. 2) The UE has not stored a valid version of a required SIB/posSIB and has not acquired SIB1 in the current modification period. 3) The UE has not stored a valid version of a required SIB/posSIB and the relevant broadcast status in the acquired SIB1 is set to 'notbroadcasting' for that SIB/posSIB in the current modification period.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.1, Acquisition of MIB and SIB1
results.model_answer: The three triggers are: (1) reception of a systemInfoModification indication, (2) reception of an ETWS indication, and (3) reception of a CMAS indication. In RRC_CONNECTED, the UE uses searchSpaceSIB1 in the active BWP to obtain the current SIB1 so that it can determine the applicable SI scheduling/value-tag information and acquire the indicated updated or warning-related SI.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2 (System information acquisition), in particular the SIB1/SI acquisition requirements for an RRC_CONNECTED UE with an active BWP configured with searchSpaceSIB1. The clause associates SIB1 acquisition with system-information-change notification and public-warning-system indications (ETWS and CMAS).

results.question: Why does a UE in RRC_IDLE initiate the procedure by transmitting an RRCSetupRequest message?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure to request the establishment of an RRC connection. The transmission of the RRCSetupRequest is the defined initial step for a UE in RRC_IDLE to transition towards RRC_CONNECTED state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3, RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: In RRC_IDLE, the UE has no established RRC connection or dedicated RRC resources. When it needs access to the network (for example, mobile-originated data/signalling or mobile-terminated access after paging), it starts RRC connection establishment by sending RRCSetupRequest on SRB0/CCCH, normally after random access. The message requests creation of an RRC connection and provides the UE identity and establishment cause, enabling the gNB to allocate/configure resources in RRCSetup. The UE then confirms completion with RRCSetupComplete.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.1.1 (RRC connection establishment, General): "The RRC connection establishment procedure is used to establish an RRC connection. The UE initiates the procedure by transmitting an RRCSetupRequest message to the network. The network responds with an RRCSetup message. The UE completes the procedure by transmitting an RRCSetupComplete message to the network."

results.question: What is the role of the RRCSetup message content in the RRC connection establishment procedure?
results.reference: The RRCSetup message provides the radio resource configuration from the network. This configuration is essential for the UE to complete the transition to RRC_CONNECTED state, as it supplies the necessary parameters for the connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3, RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: RRCSetup is the network-to-UE message that completes the initial RRC connection setup after an RRCSetupRequest. Its content provides the initial dedicated radio-resource configuration needed for the UE to enter RRC_CONNECTED, notably configuration for SRB1 and the initial cell-group/radio configuration (e.g., MAC/RLC/PHY-related configuration carried in masterCellGroup). The UE applies the configuration, establishes SRB1, and responds with RRCSetupComplete, normally carrying the initial NAS message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.2.2 (RRC setup): upon reception of RRCSetup, the UE shall perform the specified radio-resource configuration, establish SRB1, and send RRCSetupComplete. The RRCSetup message definition in clause 6.2.2 includes radioBearerConfig and masterCellGroup, which carry the initial dedicated bearer and cell-group configuration.

results.question: What action must an L2 U2N Relay UE take for a Remote UE identity in sl-RemoteUE-ToAddModList that is not currently configured?
results.reference: It must configure the parameters to the SRAP entity according to the sl-SRAP-Config-Relay.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15.2, L2 U2N Remote UE Release
results.model_answer: The L2 U2N Relay UE shall add/configure that Remote UE as a new Remote UE entry, using the associated configuration in sl-RemoteUE-ToAddModList. It must not treat the entry as a modification of an existing Remote UE configuration.
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (RRCReconfiguration reception by the UE), in the L2 U2N Relay UE handling of sl-RelayUE-Config/sl-RemoteUE-ToAddModList. The add/modify-list handling distinguishes an unconfigured Remote UE identity and requires creation/addition of its Remote UE configuration.

results.question: Under what condition does the L2 U2N Relay UE perform PC5-RRC connection release for an entry in the sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList?
results.reference: Only if the Relay UE currently has a PC5 RRC connection to an L2 U2N Remote UE with the matching sl-L2Identity-Remote value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15.2, L2 U2N Remote UE Release
results.model_answer: The L2 U2N Relay UE performs PC5-RRC connection release for a sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList entry only if it has an existing PC5-RRC connection with the Remote UE identified by that entry (i.e., the indicated remoteUE-Identity).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (RRCReconfiguration reception by the UE), in the L2 U2N Relay UE handling of sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList. The procedure states, in substance, that for each listed Remote UE, the relay releases the PC5-RRC connection if it has a PC5-RRC connection with the Remote UE indicated by the entry.

results.question: What event on the Uu interface triggers the U2N Relay UE to initiate the procedure?
results.reference: Upon experiencing a Radio Link Failure (RLF) on the Uu interface.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.10.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: Detection of a radio link failure (RLF) on the Uu interface triggers the U2N Relay UE to initiate the applicable recovery/re-establishment procedure. In particular, the relay UE treats Uu RLF as loss of its NR access link and starts RRC connection re-establishment when the re-establishment conditions are met.
results.evidence: Most likely: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.7.3 (RRC connection re-establishment — initiation). It specifies that a UE initiates RRC connection re-establishment upon AS detection of radio link failure (among other specified failure conditions). This applies equally when the UE operates as a U2N Relay UE.

results.question: Why might a UE include the last serving cell information in an RRC message during connection reestablishment?
results.reference: To provide the network with the necessary context about the cell where the failure occurred, which is required when the reestablishment procedure is initiated due to radio link failure or reconfiguration with sync failure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7, Other
results.model_answer: A UE includes its prior/source PCell identity in RRCReestablishmentRequest so the receiving gNB can associate the request with the UE's pre-failure RRC/security context. Together with the old C-RNTI and shortMAC-I, the physical cell ID identifies the cell in which that context existed, enables validation of the request, and supports recovery or retrieval of the UE context when reestablishment is attempted in another cell. It is not a general serving-cell history report.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.7.2 (Initiation of RRC connection re-establishment) and the RRCReestablishmentRequest/ReestablishmentUE-Identity ASN.1 definitions in clause 6.2. The UE is specified to populate ue-Identity with the C-RNTI used in the source PCell, the physical cell identity of the source PCell, and shortMAC-I.

results.question: What are the two specific failure scenarios that require a UE to provide last serving cell information to the network?
results.reference: The two scenarios are radio link failure and reconfiguration with sync failure, which trigger the reestablishment procedure and necessitate this information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7, Other
results.model_answer: The two failure scenarios are: (1) radio link failure (RLF), and (2) handover failure (HOF). In these cases, the UE retains/reports information associated with its last serving cell—e.g., serving-cell measurement/identity information—so the network can diagnose the connection failure and mobility outcome.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.7 (RRC re-establishment), especially the UE initiation conditions for re-establishment following radio link failure or handover failure; and clause 5.7.2 (UE information transfer), together with the RLF-Report / measResultLastServCell information-element definitions in clause 6.2.2. The RRCReestablishmentRequest also carries the old-cell physical-cell identity as part of ue-Identity for re-establishment-context identification.

results.question: How does a UE configure its associated peer UE to perform NR sidelink measurement and reporting for a unicast PC5-RRC connection?
results.reference: The UE configures the peer UE by sending an RRCReconfigurationSidelink message containing the NR sidelink measurement configuration for unicast.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: For an established unicast PC5-RRC connection, the configuring UE sends an RRCReconfigurationSidelink message to its associated peer UE. The message includes measConfig-r16 (type MeasConfigSL-r16), which adds/modifies/removes sidelink measurement objects, report configurations, measurement identities, and applicable measurement-quantity/filtering configuration. The peer UE applies the configuration, acknowledges the reconfiguration with RRCReconfigurationCompleteSidelink, performs the configured NR sidelink measurements, and sends MeasurementReportSidelink over the PC5-RRC connection when the configured periodic or event-triggered reporting criteria are met. Each report is associated with the configured measId and contains the requested sidelink measurement results.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.7 (Sidelink measurement and reporting), read with clause 5.8.3 (Sidelink RRC connection reconfiguration) and the ASN.1 definitions for RRCReconfigurationSidelink and MeasConfigSL in clause 6.3. The key normative mechanism is inclusion of measConfig-r16/MeasConfigSL-r16 in RRCReconfigurationSidelink and reporting by MeasurementReportSidelink.

results.question: What is the purpose of an NR sidelink measurement object within the configuration?
results.reference: An NR sidelink measurement object indicates the NR sidelink frequency of the reference signals that the associated peer UE must measure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: An NR sidelink measurement object (MeasObjectNR-SL) identifies and parameterizes the NR sidelink frequency/carrier on which a UE is to perform sidelink radio measurements. It provides the measurement target information used with sidelink report configurations and measurement identities, enabling the UE to evaluate sidelink signal quality/level and generate the configured measurement reports for sidelink mobility/resource-selection related procedures.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.3.2, IE MeasObjectNR-SL: the IE specifies information applicable for NR sidelink measurement. It is used in the sidelink measurement configuration together with report configurations and measurement identities.

results.question: Under what conditions does a UE apply additionalPmax from NR-NS-PmaxList upon receiving SIB2 while in RRC_IDLE?
results.reference: The UE applies additionalPmax if it is present in the same entry of the selected additionalSpectrumEmission within NR-NS-PmaxList, after having applied a supported additionalSpectrumEmission from the list.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.3, Actions upon reception of SIB2
results.model_answer: In RRC_IDLE, receipt of SIB2 causes the UE to apply additionalPmax only when NR-NS-PmaxList is present and an entry in that list is applicable to the serving NR carrier—i.e., the serving carrier's NR frequency band matches a band identified by that entry. The UE then uses that entry's signalled additionalPmax for the applicable band in the idle-mode cell-selection/reselection power-compensation calculation. A missing list, a missing/non-applicable entry, or a non-matching serving band does not trigger application of additionalPmax.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.3.1 (RRC_IDLE cell reselection—general/application of SIB2 cell-reselection parameters), together with the ASN.1 definition and field description of NR-NS-PmaxList/NR-NS-Pmax in SIB2. The normative condition is band applicability of the NR-NS-PmaxList entry, not merely successful reception of SIB2.

results.question: What is the sequence of actions a UE must take regarding NR-NS-PmaxList entries in frequencyBandList when receiving SIB2 while T311 is running?
results.reference: First, apply a supported additionalSpectrumEmission from the list; second, if additionalPmax is present in that entry, apply it; third, apply p-Max.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.3, Actions upon reception of SIB2
results.model_answer: While T311 is running, reception of SIB2 causes the UE to process the NR-NS-PmaxList as a temporary non-serving-NR maximum-power mapping. For each NR-NS-PmaxList entry, the UE associates the entry's p-Max with every NR band indicated in that entry's frequencyBandList and uses the applicable value(s) for the corresponding NR non-serving-band power-limit handling during the T311/re-establishment period. The UE does not interpret the list as a cell-reselection instruction and does not stop or restart T311 merely because SIB2 is received. The mapping is relevant only while the RLF/re-establishment procedure requiring T311 is in progress; normal serving-cell power configuration remains governed by the applicable serving-cell/SIB configuration.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.3, "RRC re-establishment" (UE behaviour while T311 is running, including processing of SIB2 information for NR-NS-PmaxList). The ASN.1 definition and field semantics are in the SIB2/NR-NS-PmaxList information-element definitions in clause 6.3.2.

results.question: How does the UE utilize the UE Positioning Assistance Information procedure regarding UL-SRS resources?
results.reference: The UE reports the association between UL-SRS resources for positioning and the UE Tx TEG ID.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.14.1, General UE Network RRCReconfiguration UEPositioningAssistanceInfo
results.model_answer: The UE uses the UE Positioning Assistance Information procedure to send the network positioning-related assistance concerning UL-SRS resources, i.e. to identify/report the UL-SRS resource information relevant to UE positioning. The network uses that information when selecting, allocating or adapting positioning SRS resources. This RRC procedure is an assistance/reporting mechanism; it does not by itself configure, reserve, grant, or trigger UL-SRS transmission. The actual UL-SRS configuration is provided by the network through the applicable RRC SRS configuration, and the UE transmits an SRS only in accordance with that configuration and its resource type/triggering rules.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.5 (UE positioning assistance information): the UE-initiated UEPositioningAssistanceInformation procedure is specified for delivery of UE positioning assistance information to the network. The associated UEPositioningAssistanceInformation message/IE definitions specify the positioning assistance content, including information applicable to UL-SRS positioning resources. The SRS configuration and UE transmission behavior are specified separately by the SRS-Config and SRS resource/resource-set definitions in TS 38.331 clause 6.3.2.

results.question: What specific relationship does the UE report in the UE Positioning Assistance Information procedure?
results.reference: It reports the association between UL-SRS resources configured for positioning purposes and the UE's Transmission Timing Error Group identifier.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.14.1, General UE Network RRCReconfiguration UEPositioningAssistanceInfo
results.model_answer: The UE reports the timing relationship between GNSS time and the NR serving-cell reference timing (i.e., the NR radio-frame/system-frame timing used as the reference). This enables the network to relate GNSS-derived time to NR time for positioning support.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3 (UE positioning assistance information procedure), together with the UEPositioningAssistanceInformation / GNSS-ReferenceTimeInfo information elements: the UE provides GNSS reference-time information expressing the relation of GNSS time to NR reference timing.

results.question: How does the network initiate a reconfiguration of sidelink communication parameters for a UE in RRC_CONNECTED?
results.reference: The network initiates the reconfiguration by sending an RRCReconfiguration message to the UE. This message contains the sl-ConfigDedicatedNR field, which provides the dedicated sidelink configuration for NR sidelink communication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1, Sidelink RRC reconfiguration
results.model_answer: For a UE in RRC_CONNECTED, the network initiates sidelink-parameter reconfiguration by transmitting an RRCReconfiguration message on SRB1. The message carries the dedicated NR sidelink configuration (e.g., sl-ConfigDedicatedNR-r16, or the applicable later-release extension), which can add, modify, or release sidelink resource/pool, bearer, and related sidelink communication settings. The UE applies the received configuration according to the RRCReconfiguration procedure and acknowledges completion with RRCReconfigurationComplete.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.1 (Sidelink communication configuration), read with clause 5.3.5 (RRC reconfiguration) and the RRCReconfiguration message definition in clause 6.2.2. The sidelink configuration is delivered as dedicated sidelink configuration information in RRCReconfiguration, including sl-ConfigDedicatedNR-r16 where applicable.

results.question: Why would a UE in RRC_CONNECTED need to apply a new sidelink configuration provided by the network?
results.reference: To establish, modify, or release sidelink radio bearers and reconfigure sidelink parameters for NR sidelink communication, as directed by the network via the dedicated configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1, Sidelink RRC reconfiguration
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED applies a new network-provided sidelink configuration because sidelink operation can be radio-resource controlled by the serving network. The new dedicated configuration may establish, modify, or release the UE's allowed sidelink operation, including applicable resource pools and associated transmission/reception parameters. Applying it ensures that sidelink use matches the current cell policy, service/QoS needs, mobility state, and interference/resource-allocation conditions, and prevents the UE from continuing to use obsolete or no-longer-authorized sidelink resources.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, "Reception of RRCReconfiguration by the UE". This procedure requires a UE to apply the configuration carried by RRCReconfiguration; sidelink-dedicated configuration is delivered as applicable RRCReconfiguration configuration content. The ASN.1 definitions/descriptions for the relevant sl-ConfigDedicatedNR / sidelink configuration IEs provide the detailed sidelink parameters affected. Exact IE placement and release-specific naming depend on the TS 38.331 release.

results.question: What specific information element within the RRCReconfiguration message carries the dedicated configuration for NR sidelink communication?
results.reference: The sl-ConfigDedicatedNR information element within the RRCReconfiguration message carries the dedicated configuration for NR sidelink communication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1, Sidelink RRC reconfiguration
results.model_answer: The dedicated NR sidelink configuration is carried by the IE `sl-ConfigDedicatedNR-r16` (type `SL-ConfigDedicatedNR-r16`) in the `RRCReconfiguration` message’s Release-16 extension IEs.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.2.2 (RRCReconfiguration message definitions), `RRCReconfiguration-v1610-IEs`: the optional field `sl-ConfigDedicatedNR-r16` is specified as the IE for configuring dedicated NR sidelink communication.

results.question: How should an IAB-node handle a received BH-RLC-ChannelConfig when a BH RLC Channel with the same bh-RLC-ChannelID already exists in the current configuration within the same cell group and the reestablishRLC indicator is received?
results.reference: The IAB-node shall re-establish the RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322, then reconfigure the RLC entity or entities according to the received rlc-Config, and reconfigure the logical channel according to the received mac-LogicalChannelConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.11, BH RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: Treat it as a modification of the existing BH RLC Channel, not as a new channel. Because the bh-RLC-ChannelID already exists in the same cell group and reestablishRLC is present, the IAB-node shall re-establish the RLC entity associated with that BH RLC Channel (i.e., reset/re-establish it according to the RLC re-establishment procedure). It shall retain the channel identity; any included rlc-Config and/or logicalChannelConfig are applied as part of the modification.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (RRCReconfiguration, IAB-node behaviour), specifically the processing rules for bh-RLC-ChannelToAddModList/BH-RLC-ChannelConfig. The relevant rule is the existing-BH-RLC-channel case: when a BH RLC Channel with the same bh-RLC-ChannelIdentity is configured in the same cell group and reestablishRLC is included, the IAB-node re-establishes the RLC entity associated with that BH RLC Channel. RLC re-establishment behaviour is specified in 3GPP TS 38.322.

results.question: What actions must an IAB-node take when it receives a BH-RLC-ChannelConfig for a bh-RLC-ChannelID that was not previously configured within the same cell group?
results.reference: The IAB-node shall establish an RLC entity in accordance with the received rlc-Config and configure this MAC entity with a logical channel according to the received mac-LogicalChannelConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.11, BH RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: For a BH-RLC-ChannelConfig whose bh-RLC-ChannelID is not already configured in the same cell group, the IAB-node shall add/configure that BH RLC channel: establish/configure the corresponding RLC entity using the provided rlc-Config and configure its associated MAC logical channel using mac-LogicalChannelConfig (when present). It is treated as an addition, not a modification or RLC re-establishment of an existing BH RLC channel.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (IAB-node handling of received RRCReconfiguration/CellGroupConfig), in the BH-RLC-ChannelConfig processing rules for bh-RLC-ChannelToAddModList. The normative branch for a bh-RLC-ChannelID not configured in the same cell group requires the IAB-node to configure the BH RLC channel/RLC entity and its MAC logical-channel configuration as applicable.

results.question: In the scenario where a BH RLC Channel with the received bh-RLC-ChannelID already exists in the current configuration within the same cell group but reestablishRLC is not received, how should the IAB-node proceed?
results.reference: The IAB-node shall reconfigure the RLC entity or entities in accordance with the received rlc-Config and reconfigure the logical channel in accordance with the received mac-LogicalChannelConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.11, BH RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: The IAB-node shall reconfigure (modify) the existing BH RLC Channel using the received bh-RLC-ChannelConfig. It shall not re-establish the RLC entity when reestablishRLC is absent, and it shall not create a second BH RLC Channel with the same bh-RLC-ChannelID in that cell group.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (IAB-node actions upon RRCReconfiguration), in the handling of bh-RLC-ChannelToAddModList / bh-RLC-ChannelConfig. The conditional handling distinguishes an already configured BH RLC Channel: presence of reestablishRLC causes RLC re-establishment; otherwise the existing BH RLC Channel is reconfigured according to the received configuration.

results.question: Why does the procedure differ when a BH-RLC-ChannelConfig is received for an existing bh-RLC-ChannelID versus a new one within the same cell group?
results.reference: For an existing BH RLC Channel, the IAB-node reconfigures or re-establishes the RLC entity and reconfigures the logical channel; for a new one, it establishes a new RLC entity and configures a new logical channel, as the actions depend on whether the backhaul logical channel was previously configured.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.11, BH RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: BH-RLC-ChannelIdentity is an identity of an RLC entity scoped to a cell group. Therefore, a received configuration with an identity already configured in that cell group is an add/modify operation on the existing entity: the IAB-MT reconfigures it, or re-establishes it when reestablishment is indicated. A previously unseen identity denotes a new RLC entity and requires establishment. This distinction prevents duplicate RLC entities for one cell-group-local identity and avoids an unintended RLC state reset for a normal modification. The same numeric identity in another cell group is not the same entity because the cell group is part of the effective scope.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, RRCReconfiguration reception/processing for IAB-MT, in the handling of BH-RLC channel add/modify configuration. The normative logic distinguishes whether the bh-RLC-ChannelIdentity corresponds to a BH-RLC channel already configured in the same cell group; it reconfigures (or re-establishes when requested) an existing RLC entity, and establishes an entity when no such identity exists.

results.question: How does a UE process the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 when it receives this list?
results.reference: The UE processes each sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 in the received list that is part of its current sidelink configuration by releasing both the RLC entity and the corresponding logical channel associated with that identifier.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.1, PC5 Relay RLC channel release
results.model_answer: For each sl-RLC-ChannelIdentity in sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5, the UE releases the associated sidelink RLC entity, if one exists, and releases/removes the corresponding MAC logical-channel configuration, if one exists. The list is processed per identity; it does not imply release of unrelated RLC channels or bearers.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (UE actions on RRCReconfiguration), in the sidelink/PC5 RLC-channel configuration processing text. The associated ASN.1 IE definition is in clause 6.3.2 under SL-RLC-ChannelConfigPC5, where sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 is a list of SL-RLC-ChannelIdentity values.

results.question: What specific actions must a UE take for an sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 included in the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5?
results.reference: For each such identifier that is part of the current UE sidelink configuration, the UE must release the RLC entity and the corresponding logical channel associated with that sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.1, PC5 Relay RLC channel release
results.model_answer: For each sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 in sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5, the UE shall: (1) release the RLC entity associated with that sidelink RLC channel ID; and (2) release the MAC logical channel associated with that sidelink RLC channel ID.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (actions upon reception of RRCReconfiguration, sidelink/PC5 RLC-channel configuration processing): for every sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 in sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5, the UE releases the associated RLC entity and the associated MAC logical channel.
